hodge-conjecture.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties' (OpenAI, dated October 7, 2026; the README notes it supersedes a September 23, 2026 version by updating one citation). Its main theorem (thm:main) takes an abelian variety A over Q̄ of dimension d with good reduction A_0 over F̄ₚ at a p-adic place w, a rational Hodge class γ in H^{2r}(A(C), Q(r)), and any Cartier divisors D_1,...,D_{d-r} on A_0. It shows that the traces of γ_0 against the divisor products are one rational number q in every ℓ-adic realization (ℓ ≠ p) and in crystalline cohomology. The corollary 'Algebraic specialization of rational Hodge classes' goes further: there is one rational algebraic cycle z_γ in CH^r(A_0)⊗Q, on the special fibre over F̄ₚ, whose ℓ-adic and crystalline cycle classes equal those of γ_0. Its proof transports γ to a CM abelian variety B by a quasi-isogeny of special fibres, and then uses the companion OpenAI manuscript 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (cited as OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1) to say that the CM class is algebraic.
hodge-conjecture.revisions: 1 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Milnes-rationality-conjecture-for-abelian-varieties-September-23-2026
hodge-conjecture.delivers: Algebraicity in characteristic p, for every residue characteristic p including 2, of the specializations at one fixed good-reduction place of rational Hodge classes on abelian varieties over Q̄, in every degree 2r. The cycles live on the reduction A_0 over F̄ₚ, not on A(C). The manuscript does not claim to settle the Hodge conjecture. It says the corollary 'neither asserts the Hodge conjecture for arbitrary abelian varieties in characteristic zero nor lifts z_γ to the original generic fiber'. The only characteristic-zero algebraicity it uses is the CM case from OpenAICMHodge2026, which this family does not prove. None of the statement about complex projective manifolds is addressed.
hodge-conjecture.remains: All of what the list asks: for every non-singular complex projective X, every rational Hodge class is a rational linear combination of classes of complex subvarieties. Left open even for abelian varieties: for a given rational Hodge class on A(C) the family produces no algebraic cycle on A(C), and it produces nothing in characteristic zero for non-CM abelian varieties or for any other variety.
hodge-conjecture.doubts: (1) The abstract says every specialized Hodge class 'is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle' and does not say that the cycle lies on the reduction over F̄ₚ. The body makes that restriction and disclaims the characteristic-zero Hodge conjecture. (2) The algebraicity statement is an explicit additional input from the companion manuscript; the authors say the main theorem does not need it. (3) The text flags no step as sketched, but the proof is long and relies on several cited inputs that the authors state rather than prove.; conditional on: The algebraic-specialization corollary depends on OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1 (the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, a companion OpenAI manuscript not read here). The main theorem's proof is stated to be independent of it. The construction also cites external results without proving them: Kisin–Zhou (2025, preprint), Pappas–Rapoport (2024), Gleason–Lim–Xu (Invent. Math. 2026, Corollary 6.3, for a uniformization condition), Milne (2009, Theorem 4.5), Deligne (1982), Blasius (1994) and Moonen (1998).
hodge-conjecture.direction: proves algebraicity in characteristic p of specialized Hodge classes; the conjecture itself is not addressed

hodge-conjecture.what_happened: Four of the five manuscripts claim the rational Hodge conjecture (HC) for specified classes of varieties; the fifth is a conditional reduction and proves no HC case. (1) 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) claims that for every complex CM abelian variety A and every p, the cycle class map CH^p(A)_Q -> H^{2p}(A,Q) ∩ H^{p,p}(A) is surjective (Theorem thm:cm), hence HC in every codimension on every finite product of CM abelian varieties and on their powers. It also claims the generalized HC for CM abelian varieties (Corollary cc:ghc), via Hazama and Abdulali. The proof is a Hodge-theoretic construction: theta one-forms on a compact ball quotient, Hecke and Frobenius arithmetic, and a four-factor surface criterion. (2) 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers' (6 Oct) claims HC in every codimension on every self-power A^m, m >= 1, for two classes: complex abelian sixfolds with an imaginary-quadratic action whose rational Hermitian form is hyperbolic of signature (3,3) (Theorem p3ab:split-sixfolds), and complex abelian varieties of dimension at most five with an imaginary-quadratic action (Theorem p3ab:quadratic-five). Both allow nonsimple varieties and special periods. Its key tensor criterion (Theorem p3:tensor-criterion) reduces Hodge tensors to determinant lines supplied by CM cycles and by a Weil-plane input (Theorem p3sw:weil-plane), which the text proves by following Markman's construction. (3) 'Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers' (6 Oct) claims HC in every codimension for (i) self-powers of the Jacobian of a connected abelian cover of curves at each point s of a complement of a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of the marked parameter space, and for products of such a Jacobian with a CM abelian variety (Theorem p4:abelian-covers); and (ii) self-powers of very general smooth diagonal complete intersections X_A in P^{d+c} of dimension d, cut out by c <= 2 equations of common degree n >= 2, for every d (Theorem thm:main). (4) 'Algebraic Kuga-Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus' (30 Sep) claims HC and the generalized HC in every degree for every self-power S^m of a projective K3 surface S that admits a rational isometric embedding (T_S,q) into V_P, with V_P = U_Q^{+2} ⊥ <-1>^4 (Theorem main:theorem). This includes every ample P-polarized K3, P = U ⊕ D8(-1) ⊕ D4(-1). It also states the general criterion (Theorem ext:criterion): algebraicity of one exact even-Clifford Kuga-Satake tensor on any projective K3 implies HC and GHC for every self-power. Corollary transfer:moduli extends these to Hilbert schemes of points and certain moduli spaces. (5) 'A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga-Satake Correspondences' (10 Sep) proves no HC case. At a K3 point with full orthogonal Hodge group, existence of any one nonzero algebraic correspondence from primitive H^2 of the K3 to H^2 of an abelian variety is equivalent to algebraicity of the prescribed full Kuga-Satake correspondence (Theorem main:generic). If that existence holds very generally in a polarized component, the prescribed correspondence is algebraic throughout the component (Theorem main:specialization). The existence input is stated as unproven.
hodge-conjecture.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-September-30-2026, Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-September-30-2026, Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-September-30-2026
hodge-conjecture.delivers: Establishes HC (rational coefficients, algebraic cycle classes, every degree) only for the listed classes: CM abelian varieties and their finite products and powers; all self-powers of the split (3,3) sixfolds and of abelian varieties of dimension at most five with an imaginary-quadratic action; all self-powers of abelian-cover Jacobians at generic markings, and of their products with CM abelian varieties; self-powers of very general diagonal complete intersections of the stated type; all self-powers of K3 surfaces with a rational isometric embedding of T_S into V_P, plus Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces of those K3s. Since dim V_P = 8, that hypothesis forces rank T_S <= 8, i.e. Picard number >= 14 (my reading of the hypothesis). The generalized HC is claimed only for CM abelian varieties and for the K3 self-powers (including Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces); the other manuscripts claim HC alone. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the general problem as the bullet states it (every smooth projective complex X, any dimension, any degree). For the CM paper, the statement matches the list's (rational coefficients, complex-subvariety cycles, all degrees) but restricted to CM abelian varieties. The Sept 10 manuscript delivers no unconditional HC result.
hodge-conjecture.remains: HC for smooth projective complex varieties in general. For abelian varieties: all non-CM ones outside the listed quadratic-action and (3,3)-sixfold classes, including general abelian varieties of dimension six or more. For K3 surfaces: those whose transcendental quadratic space does not rationally embed in V_P, unless the criterion's exact tensor is shown algebraic. For abelian-cover Jacobians: the non-generic markings. For diagonal complete intersections with c = 2: the exceptional locus, per the theorem's statement. The generalized HC beyond the listed cases. The existence of the initial Kuga-Satake correspondence at any point, which the Sept 10 manuscript leaves as the external input.
hodge-conjecture.doubts: The CM manuscript is about 4,100 lines of section text. I read its introduction, consequences section and assembly, and only excerpts of the theta and Hecke sections (04, 05), so those proofs are not checked. In the theta section the text disclaims some properties at intermediate parameters (holomorphy; splitting over every unitary group) and works only with the restricted statements. The Weil manuscript's Weil-plane theorem is the same statement Markman claims (Markman 2025 Theorem 1.5.1; Markman 2026 Theorem 1.2), and the text calls its geometric proof 'a detailed treatment of Markman's construction'; the claimed new content is the all-powers step. Its dimension-five case analysis (Types I-IV, remainder cases) is terse. The n < 6 determinant supply (Lemma p3ab:determinant-supply, case 2) is said to come from adding CM elliptic factors, which I did not verify. The abelian-cover manuscript's abstract says 'very general' for the diagonal family, but its Theorem thm:main states that for c <= 1 or d = 0 no exceptional set is needed, so for those cases it claims every smooth parameter. The text also notes that a cited moduli discussion (Gonzalez-Diez-Hidalgo-Leyton, Section 4.2) assumes (m-2)(n-1) > 2, and says its own Section sec:family supplies the needed family, including the genus-zero and elliptic boundary cases. I did not verify that section, nor its positive-genus and sphere character analysis. The K3 manuscript's extension to all periods uses Baire and analytic-set arguments (Lemma specialization:ambient) and a rational period transfer through Buskin's theorem. Its middle sections (double covers, Gauss pencil, the uniruled-threefold comparison) are long and I did not verify them. Its introduction claims more than the abstract: HC and GHC extend to Hilbert schemes and moduli spaces via motivic decompositions. The Sept 10 manuscript is conditional by design; its unconditional content is the equivalence in Theorem main:generic.; conditional on: Within this family: the CM Hodge theorem (Theorem thm:cm of 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', cited as OpenAICM2026 or OpenAICM) is the only Hodge-conjecture input of 'Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers' (its Lemma p3:cm-operations) and of 'Abelian covers, Gale correspondences...' (through its companion results). The abelian-cover manuscript also uses the companion results of the Weil manuscript (its Section 2 tools, Theorem 2.5 saturated criterion, Lemma 2.6 correspondence transfer; the text says 'their proofs belong to the companion paper'). The Weil manuscript's Weil-plane input (Theorem p3sw:weil-plane) is proved in the text, but it follows Markman's construction and cites Markman's lemmas (Markman 2025, Section 7.4.2 and Lemmas 9.3.2, 9.3.11; Markman 2026, Sections 11.3-11.5), plus Buchweitz-Flenner and Caldararu-type Hochschild results. The abelian-cover exceptional loci rely on Cattani-Deligne-Kaplan (algebraicity of Hodge loci, arXiv 1994) and on Shioda-Katsura Fermat domination. The K3 manuscript relies on external results: Buskin (algebraicity of rational Hodge isometries of K3 surfaces), Varesco (powers of K3 surfaces and similarities), Zarhin, and, for Corollary transfer:moduli, de Cataldo-Migliorini, Bulles, Arapura and Riess. Its conditional criterion (Theorem ext:criterion) needs one exact cycle; Theorem main:theorem supplies that cycle on the V_P locus. The Sept 10 manuscript is conditional on the existence of one very generally nonzero algebraic correspondence, which it calls the external existence problem. The CM manuscript's specialization remark depends on a separate companion, 'Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties' (7 Oct), which I did not read; the text says that remark is not an input to the main theorem.
hodge-conjecture.direction: proves the conjecture for special classes of varieties (CM abelian varieties; several families of self-powers); conditional reduction for Kuga-Satake algebraicity
hodge-conjecture.object: No counterexample. The Gale correspondence in the diagonal complete intersection manuscript is an explicit algebraic correspondence (a perfect tensor between the two character spaces, pulled back to a Fermat hypersurface F_n^{m-2}). The cycles for CM classes are not written out: they come from a compact ball-quotient construction and an existence-type surface criterion. The K3 correspondence Gamma_S is built from double covers of abelian surfaces, Gauss pencils and a degree-three Hodge comparison, not written down explicitly.

tate-conjecture.what_happened: Same manuscript, same corollary 'Algebraic specialization of rational Hodge classes'. For each rational Hodge class γ on A(C), with A over Q̄ abelian and good reduction at w, it produces z_γ in CH^r(A_0)⊗Q on the special fibre over F̄ₚ with cl_ℓ(z_γ) = γ_{0,ℓ} for every ℓ ≠ p. So the ℓ-adic realization of every specialized Hodge class lies in the image of the cycle map with Q coefficients. The manuscript does not state Tate's conjecture and does not discuss Galois invariance or descent to a finite field.
tate-conjecture.revisions: 1 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Milnes-rationality-conjecture-for-abelian-varieties-September-23-2026
tate-conjecture.delivers: Algebraicity over F̄ₚ of ℓ-adic classes that are specializations of rational Hodge classes on abelian varieties over Q̄ with good reduction at w. Tate's conjecture concerns Galois-invariant classes over finitely generated fields and asks that they be spanned by algebraic cycles. The family does not show that the classes it covers are Galois-invariant, does not show that the cycles can be taken over a finite field, and does not treat Tate's second conjecture. It therefore does not settle Tate's conjecture in any case as the list states it. At most it covers a restricted class of ℓ-adic classes, over an algebraic closure, and the manuscript does not present this as a case of Tate's conjecture.
tate-conjecture.remains: Tate's first conjecture for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields in all codimensions, including divisors. Galois invariance and descent to finite fields for the classes the family covers. Tate's second conjecture. All varieties other than abelian varieties with good reduction at w over Q̄, and the strong (semisimplicity) form.
tate-conjecture.doubts: The text does not show that the specialized ℓ-adic classes are Galois-invariant, which is the hypothesis Tate's conjecture needs. The cycle z_γ is built over F̄ₚ, and the text does not say it is defined over any finite field. Right after the fixed-theory corollary, the text says that result 'alone gives no algebraic cycle and proves neither the Hodge nor the Tate conjecture'. The algebraic-specialization corollary is a separate claim and is not discussed in those terms.; conditional on: OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1, as for the Hodge entry: the CM class κ is algebraic only by that companion result.
tate-conjecture.direction: proves algebraicity over F̄ₚ of specialized Hodge classes; Tate's conjecture not addressed

tate-conjecture.what_happened: Only 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) addresses this. Its Corollary cc:tate claims that for every abelian variety A over a finite field F_q, every r >= 0 and every prime l different from char(F_q), the cycle class map CH^r(A) ⊗ Q_l -> H^{2r}_et(A-bar, Q_l(r))^{G_q} is surjective, where G_q = Gal(F_q-bar/F_q). The same corollary states that numerical equivalence and l-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A-bar. The proof applies Milne's Theorem 7.1 and formulation (0.1) of Milne 1999 ('Lefschetz motives and the Tate conjecture'), with the author's correction. It then passes from geometric cycles to cycles over F_q by a finite pushforward and division by m.
tate-conjecture.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-September-30-2026, Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-September-30-2026, Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-September-30-2026
tate-conjecture.delivers: Tate's first conjecture, in the form stated (surjectivity of the l-adic cycle class map onto the Galois-invariant part, rational coefficients, every codimension, every l different from the characteristic), for all abelian varieties over finite fields. That is the abelian-variety, finite-field case of the bullet's question. It does not reach the general statement for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields, and it does not address Tate's second conjecture (rank of algebraic cycles modulo homological equivalence against the order of the pole of the L-function at s = r). The manuscript does not claim to settle the bullet.
tate-conjecture.remains: Tate's first conjecture for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields other than abelian varieties over finite fields, including abelian varieties over number fields, K3 surfaces and other varieties, and the divisor case beyond abelian varieties. Tate's second conjecture, for every variety. Integral and strong (semisimplicity) variants are outside the bullet and are not treated.
tate-conjecture.doubts: The corollary relies on a published theorem of Milne whose auxiliary-field choice the text says needs correcting; the correction is an externally hosted author's note, which I did not read. The text itself says Milne's implication does not assert that each Tate class lifts to a Hodge class on a single CM lift. No step is flagged as sketched in the corollary or its proof.; conditional on: Milne's Theorem 7.1 and formulation (0.1) of Milne 1999 (Compositio Mathematica 117), read with the author's correction page (cc:Milne1999Addenda, hosted at jmilne.org; not in the repository). The text says the hypothesis of Milne's theorem is supplied by the paper's own CM Hodge theorem (Theorem thm:cm). No companion manuscript is needed for this corollary.
tate-conjecture.direction: proves the conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields (all codimensions, all l different from p)

birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.what_happened: Three manuscripts in this family bear on BSD, with nested scope. (1) 'Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' (dated 7 Oct 2026) claims: for every E/ℚ and every prime q with s_q(E) in {0,1}, where s_q(E) is the ℤ_q-corank of the full q-power Selmer group, the algebraic rank, the analytic rank and s_q(E) all coincide, Sha(E/ℚ) is finite, and the full leading-term formula L⁽ʳ⁾(E,1)/r! = Ω_E·Reg_E·#Sha(E/ℚ)·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E) / #E(ℚ)_tors² holds, with no hypotheses on reduction, torsion, isogeny, CM or residual representation. The rank and finiteness statements are taken from (2) and the two-primary equality from (3); the paper's own new content is the exact valuation at every odd prime, obtained from a pair identity over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic twist, a one-sided nonnegativity inequality for non-CM curves, a unit comparison, and a separate CM argument. (2) 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime' (dated 7 Oct 2026) claims: for every E/ℚ, every prime p and r in {0,1}, s_p(E)=r implies analytic rank = Mordell–Weil rank = r and #Sha(E/ℚ) < ∞. It says nothing about the leading coefficient. Its odd-prime argument is by contradiction from an assumed torsion Heegner point, through theta series on a unitary group, cusp lifting and Galois extraction. As an application it claims that for every prime ℓ ≡ 4,7,8 (mod 9) the cubic X³+Y³=ℓZ³ has analytic and Mordell–Weil rank one and finite Sha, hence every such ℓ is a sum of two rational cubes; the text says Yin and Burungale–Tian had these cases already. (3) 'The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one' (dated 6 Oct 2026) claims: for E/ℚ with s_2(E) ≤ 1, rank = analytic rank = s_2(E), Sha finite, and Q_E = L⁽ʳ⁾(E,1)·(#E_tors)² / (r!·Ω_E·Reg_E·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)) is a positive rational with v₂(Q_E) = v₂(#Sha). Its corollary gives the same conclusions for any E with some s_p(E) ≤ 1, and a density statement: for a fixed curve, on a density-one set of signed squarefree twists, the twists have s_2 equal to 0 or 1, each value having density one half, with the two-primary formula holding for them.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-3-2026, The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-September-24-2026, The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-September-24-2026
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.delivers: For curves E/ℚ with some p-Selmer corank ≤ 1, the claims cover all three parts of the list's conjecture: part (1), equality of algebraic and analytic rank; part (2), the leading-term formula; part (3), finiteness of Sha. The formula in (1) uses the list's constants with normalizations the paper states: Ω_E integrates |ω_E| over all real components of E(ℝ), with ω_E a global minimal Néron differential; c_ℓ(E) = [E(ℚ_ℓ):E₀(ℚ_ℓ)] at every finite prime; Reg_E is the determinant of B(P,Q) = (H(P+Q)−H(P)−H(Q))/2 on a basis of E(ℚ)/torsion, with H(P) = lim 4^(−n) log max(|a|,b) for x(2ⁿP) = a/b, which is the canonical height attached to 2[O] (twice the one attached to [O]); Reg_E = 1 in rank 0, and an index-m sublattice multiplies it by m². L(E,s) is the full Hasse–Weil L-function with its bad Euler factors. The list does not fix these conventions, so the match holds under the paper's stated ones. Scope: the covered class is curves with some s_p ≤ 1 at some prime p. Since s_p(E) ≥ rank E(ℚ) for every p, by the Kummer sequence, no curve of rank ≥ 2 is covered. Manuscript (3) by itself proves only the 2-primary part. Each twist in its density-one set has s_2 ≤ 1, so manuscript (1) applies to each, which would give the full formula on that set; neither manuscript states this combination.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.remains: Curves E/ℚ whose p-Selmer coranks are all ≥ 2 are untouched by all three manuscripts. This includes every curve of Mordell–Weil rank ≥ 2. For these, rank equality, the leading-term formula and finiteness of Sha all remain open. Among curves of rank 0 or 1, those with s_p ≥ 2 for every prime p also remain open. Not addressed: the number-field form given in the Wikipedia lead, and the abelian-variety form in the Clay statement. Within the covered class the text claims nothing remains.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.doubts: The texts flag no step as sketched and state no hedges. Points bearing on trust: (a) The odd-prime argument of (1), in its Sections 5 to 9, is the bulk of the paper. I read only its introduction, Section 2 and the assembly in Section 10, not those proofs. The introduction names the passage from an integral quotient to an exact unit at the central point, by theta constructions with growing p-level and removal of quotient divisors by added tame variables, as the step that makes the central comparison exact. (b) The rank-zero CM lemma in (1) is short. It asserts that after an isogeny the Burungale–Flach hypotheses hold, says the non-maximal-order case is supplied by a preceding lattice argument, and cites the descent step to Burungale–Flach Corollary 2. (c) The CM leading-coefficient corollary in (3) is condensed. It says the same calculation 'in the period-normalized sense' gives the claim, and handles elements needing denominators by passing to a multiple and 'homogeneity'. (d) The density corollary in (3) takes its Selmer-corank input from the proof, not the stated form, of Theorem 1.2 of the Goldfeld manuscript, whose stated theorem is about analytic rank.; conditional on: Manuscript (1) takes rank and finiteness from manuscript (2) and the two-primary equality from manuscript (3). Those are separate manuscripts of this family and (1) does not prove them. Manuscripts (1), (2) and (3) choose their auxiliary imaginary quadratic fields with the twist-density theorem of 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (OpenAI); manuscript (2) also takes its p = 2 case from that manuscript, and (3) uses the proof of its Theorem 1.2 for the density corollary. The CM case of (1) uses Burungale–Flach's exact BSD theorem for CM curves with nonvanishing L-value at 1 (their Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1), applied after an isogeny. The CM comparison in (3) uses Burungale–Flach's machinery (their Proposition 3.1, Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.1) and Kato's reciprocity law. Classical inputs include Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, modularity, and Cassels–Milne isogeny invariance.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.direction: proves the full conjecture (all three parts, with the list's constants) for the subclass of curves with some p-Selmer corank ≤ 1; the two-primary manuscript proves only the 2-primary part of the leading term

birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.what_happened: Manuscript 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion' (paper.tex, dated October 7, 2026) claims Theorem 1.1 (thm:main): for E/Q with E(Q)[2] nonzero and s_2(E) = corank over Z_2 of Sel_{2^infinity}(E/Q) equal to 0 or 1, ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank_Z E(Q) = s_2(E), and Sha(E/Q) is finite. The method builds integral interpolation families of quadratic twists, using cyclotomic classes (Kato), Heegner and ring-class deformations, and finite prime networks, and recovers the value or derivative at the given curve. For analytic order 0 or 1 the manuscript uses the published Gross-Zagier and Kolyvagin theorems to pass from analytic order to rank and finiteness of Sha. The introduction says the broader companion 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse' (cited as OpenAIGoldfeldTwoConverse2026) is not an input to this proof. The Hilbert manuscript in this family does not bear on BSD.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-September-24-2026, A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-September-24-2026
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.delivers: For the subclass of curves with nonzero rational two-torsion and s_2 at most one, the theorem gives: (1) the rank part, ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank E(Q), since both equal s_2; and (3) finiteness of Sha(E/Q). It covers CM and non-CM curves, every rational isogeny configuration, and every reduction type at 2 and at the bad primes, as the text says. Since s_2 is at least the rank, this subclass has algebraic rank at most one; the new content is the direction from Selmer corank to analytic order, while the direction from analytic order at most one to rank is Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin. Part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, is not addressed: the text says it 'does not assert the full Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula'. The matching pass's summary ('Selmer corank at most one gives equal analytic and Mordell-Weil rank and finite Sha') leaves out the hypothesis E(Q)[2] nonzero, which the theorem requires. The bullet asks about every elliptic curve over Q; the manuscript does not claim that.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.remains: (a) Curves over Q with no rational two-torsion point, for parts (1) and (3). (b) Curves with s_2 at least 2; this includes every curve of algebraic rank at least 2, since rank is at most s_2. (c) Part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, for every curve, including the subclass: the Tamagawa product, the regulator, the order of Sha and the torsion order are not shown to match the leading Taylor coefficient. (d) For the subclass, part (3) is proved, but the leading-term formula in (2) still needs (c).

birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts in the family. (a) 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) claims three things. First, the 2-converse: for every E/Q whose full 2^∞-Selmer corank c₂(E) (local Kummer conditions at every place) is 0 or 1, ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = rank E(Q) = c₂(E), and Sha(E/Q) is finite. The proof splits into the case E(Q)[2] ≠ 0 and the case E[2] irreducible. Second, a finite-descent corollary: if d₂(E) = dim Sel₂(E/Q) − dim E(Q)[2] is 0 or 1, the same equalities hold and Sha(E/Q)[2^∞] = 0. Third, a density theorem: for every E/Q, the signed squarefree twist parameters d with analytic rank 0 and with analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2 among signed squarefree d ordered by |d|; for a density-one set of such d, analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks of E^(d) agree and Sha(E^(d)/Q) is finite. (b) 'The mean analytic rank of quadratic twists of elliptic curves' (The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026) proves that the mean analytic rank of the twists E^(d) tends to 1/2 in the same ordering. It takes the density theorem of (a) as its only input from (a) and adds its own tail estimate. It is about twists, not E itself, and says nothing about the leading coefficient.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026, The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.delivers: For every E/Q with c₂(E) ∈ {0,1}, with no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, rational torsion or rational isogeny, the manuscript establishes part (1), that algebraic rank equals the analytic order of vanishing, and part (3), finiteness of Sha(E/Q). The restriction that matters is c₂(E) ≤ 1, a bound on the full 2-power Selmer corank, not on the rank alone. For a general E, the density theorem gives rank equality and finiteness only for a density-one set of quadratic twists E^(d), not for E itself. The manuscript says its rank and finiteness assertions 'are distinct from the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula', so part (2), the leading-coefficient formula, is not established here. The introduction also cites a separate preprint, OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026 (Corollary 16.1), which with the density theorem gives the two-primary leading-coefficient formula on a density-one set of signed squarefree twists; the manuscript says this leading-coefficient assertion concerns the valuation at 2 only. That preprint is not in this family and is not read here. Neither manuscript says it settles Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct: (a) for every E/Q with c₂(E) ≥ 2, including every E whose 2-Selmer corank is at least two, equality of ord_{s=1}L(E,s) and rank E(Q) and finiteness of Sha(E/Q) are not addressed; (b) the leading-coefficient formula L^(r)(E,1)/r! = Ω_E · Reg_E · #Sha(E/Q) · ∏c_p / #E(Q)_tors² is not addressed for any E, beyond the 2-adic-valuation consequence on a density-one set of twists attributed to the other preprint; (c) in the list's own words, for E itself the statement is open whenever c₂(E) ≥ 2.
birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture.doubts: (1) The rank statement is restricted to c₂(E) ≤ 1 and says nothing for E with c₂(E) ≥ 2; the manuscripts do not present themselves as settling Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer. (2) The leading-coefficient consequence is attributed to another preprint and, in this text, is only a 2-adic valuation statement about twists. (3) Without marking any step as sketched, the text flags its delicate points. In the irreducible-E[2] construction the coefficient test 'does not identify the coefficient test with the determinant' and is linked to it only by a sum-zero relation. The odd-sign coefficient selection is described as a minimum over bounded-weight sequences as precision grows, with each finite collection of tests 'realized at a sufficiently high actual precision'. (4) The proof runs to about 9,300 lines of TeX across the section files. Reader's note, not a claim of the text: I read the statements, the reduction steps and some of the constructions, not all of them, so I have not checked the middle sections.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in the 2-converse or in the density theorem as stated, and BSD is not assumed; the Heegner-section proof says 'no BSD equality is assumed'. Monsky, Cassels and Tate are cited for 2-descent parity and isogeny invariance. (iii) The two-primary leading-coefficient consequence in the introduction depends on OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026 (Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 16.1), a different manuscript that is not read here. The proof sections of this manuscript cite no other OpenAI manuscript. The mean-rank manuscript uses the density theorem only for its mean result.

congruent-number-problem.what_happened: None of the three manuscripts mentions congruent numbers, Tunnell's theorem or rational right triangles. The bearing is indirect, through 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime'. For squarefree n > 0, the congruent-number curve is E_n: y² = x³ − n²x, and n is congruent exactly when rank E_n(ℚ) ≥ 1. That manuscript's theorem gives rank E_n(ℚ) = s_p(E_n) whenever some p-Selmer corank s_p(E_n) is ≤ 1. The manuscripts do not draw this consequence. The sum-of-two-cubes corollary in the same manuscript concerns X³+Y³=ℓZ³ and not congruent numbers, so the matching note's stated reason does not supply the bearing; the bearing is the rank statement above. 'Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' also covers E_n whenever some s_q(E_n) ≤ 1, with the full leading-term formula, but does not mention congruent numbers or Tunnell's criterion.
congruent-number-problem.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-3-2026, The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-September-24-2026, The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-September-24-2026
congruent-number-problem.delivers: No determination of congruent numbers is claimed. The consequence the Selmer converse yields, which the text does not state: for each squarefree n for which some Selmer corank of E_n is ≤ 1, n is congruent if and only if that corank equals 1. A corank of 0 shows n is not congruent; a corank of 1 shows it is. This decides only those n, through a Selmer-based test that requires the coranks to be computed. It gives nothing for an n whose Selmer coranks are all ≥ 2. The problem's request for a precise characterisation is not met, and no Tunnell-type criterion appears in the manuscripts.
congruent-number-problem.remains: For n whose E_n has every p-Selmer corank ≥ 2 (this includes every n whose E_n has rank ≥ 2), these results leave open whether n is congruent. The characterisation for all n is not given. Whether the determination is unconditional is open in the sense that it depends on the Goldfeld manuscript (see conditional_on). The text does not discuss the literal wording 'rational numbers' against squarefree integers; E_n depends on n only up to squares over ℚ, so the reduction to squarefree n is harmless but unstated.
congruent-number-problem.doubts: The congruent-number implication is my deduction from the Selmer converse's theorem. No manuscript states it, and none checks the translation to individual n. The matching note's reason (sum of two cubes) is a statement about X³+Y³=ℓZ³, not about congruent numbers. No manuscript computes any Selmer corank of an E_n.; conditional on: The implication rests on 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime', which at p = 2 and for its auxiliary-field choice depends on 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (OpenAI, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2). That manuscript is not among the files I read, so I have not checked it.

congruent-number-problem.what_happened: Neither manuscript mentions congruent numbers or Tunnell's theorem. The link runs through E₀: y² = x³ − x. Its twist by a squarefree d is E₀^(d): d·y² = x³ − x, which over Q is y² = x³ − d²x (substitute X = dx, Y = d²y). For n > 0 squarefree this is the congruent-number curve E_n: y² = x³ − n²x. Both manuscripts apply to E₀ as they apply to any E/Q. The Goldfeld-density manuscript (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) gives the 2-converse and the density theorem described under the BSD entry. The mean-rank manuscript (The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026) gives mean analytic rank 1/2 over signed squarefree twists of E₀. The following is my derivation from those theorems. It is not stated in either manuscript. (i) Because E₀^(n) and E₀^(−n) are the same curve, the signed counts split evenly between positive and negative n, so the density statements hold over positive squarefree n with the same values: analytic rank 0 and analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2, and c₂ ∈ {0,1} has density one. (ii) For positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the 2-converse gives ord_{s=1}L(E_n,s) = rank E_n(Q) = c₂(E_n). Since n is congruent exactly when E_n(Q) has positive rank (the standard equivalence for squarefree n, where E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²), we get: n is congruent ⇔ c₂(E_n) = 1 ⇔ L(E_n,1) = 0. No BSD assumption is used. The classical Tunnell route needs BSD for the step 'L(E_n,1) = 0 implies n congruent'; for n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1} this manuscript supplies that step unconditionally. (iii) The set of n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 has density zero, since Smith's count, which the Goldfeld manuscript uses, makes c₂ ∈ {0,1} density one. Together with (i) and (ii), this gives that congruent numbers have asymptotic density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers.
congruent-number-problem.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026, The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026
congruent-number-problem.delivers: Restricted to positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the family decides congruence unconditionally, with 'congruent' equal to 'L(E_n,1) = 0' and to '2-Selmer corank 1' (step ii above). The family's own statements give density 1/2 for analytic rank 0 and for analytic rank 1 among the twists of E₀, and by (i) and (iii), density 1/2 for congruent numbers among positive squarefree integers. These are asymptotic statements. They do not say whether any particular n is congruent, and they do not give a procedure that decides every n. The problem asks to 'determine precisely what rational numbers are congruent numbers'. This family does not meet that demand, which needs a criterion for every n.
congruent-number-problem.remains: (a) A criterion that decides every n. For n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 nothing is said, and the family gives no computation of c₂(E_n) for any particular n. (b) The density-zero exceptional set where c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 is not resolved. (c) Tunnell's L-value criterion is neither stated nor proved in these manuscripts, so the problem's named route is not reproduced here. (d) Non-integral rationals: the manuscripts say nothing about them. The reduction to positive squarefree integers is the literature's convention, and the problem's literal 'rational numbers' wording is not addressed.
congruent-number-problem.doubts: (1) No manuscript mentions congruent numbers, Tunnell's theorem, or the density of congruent numbers. Steps (i) to (iii) are my derivation from the stated theorems and should be weighed as such. (2) The density theorems are stated for the signed count. The reduction to positive n uses E₀^(n) = E₀^(−n), which I checked from the twist formula; the manuscripts do not state it. (3) The Goldfeld manuscript's introduction cites congruent-number literature (Tian; Smith; Kriz; and BurungaleTian2026, Theorem 1.2, which gives rank zero for almost all positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8 in the family n·y² = x³ − x). These are cited as background, and the family does not rely on them. (4) The density statements are asymptotic, and nothing in the text says which n are congruent.; conditional on: Step (ii) uses the 2-converse for E_n, which applies only where c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}; the manuscripts give no way to check that for a given n. The density statements use Smith2025 Theorem 1.1 (external, not reproved here). The facts 'congruent ⇔ positive rank for squarefree n' and 'E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²' are standard results used from outside the family. The rest of the dependencies are as in the BSD entry: Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, Kato, Waldspurger, Howard, Monsky and Cassels.

riemann-hypothesis.what_happened: Two manuscripts claim zero-free half-planes for zeta. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that every finite-order Hecke L-function over Q(√-3) and every Dirichlet L-function, zeta included, has no zero with Re s > 7/8, with the principal pole at s=1 allowed. Its Part I proves the same statement with 11/12 in place of 7/8 (Theorem 'The 11/12 half-plane'), and Part II builds on that. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims the weaker half-plane Re s > 11/12 for the same families, by a route through a mean-square bound for twisted Möbius sums; it describes the 7/8 result as stronger. For zeta, the claim is that every nontrivial zero has real part at most 7/8 (Sept 30) or at most 11/12 (Oct 5).
riemann-hypothesis.delivers: A fixed zero-free strip next to the line Re s = 1 for zeta: no nontrivial zero with real part in (7/8, 1) according to Sept 30, or in (11/12, 1) according to Oct 5. Zeros with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12) are not restricted to any line, so the location question is not decided. The Sept 30 introduction says that the theorem does not establish the Riemann hypothesis or its generalized versions.
riemann-hypothesis.remains: That every nontrivial zero of zeta with 0 < Re s ≤ 7/8 (or ≤ 11/12) has real part exactly 1/2. The list's universal claim is otherwise untouched.

machine_checked.scope:
The quasi-Riemann hypothesis asks for a fixed zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$ with $\theta<1$. The formalization gives $\theta=7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function, uniformly over all positive moduli and all characters. It also establishes the same bound for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.

The principal-character poles at $s=1$ are excluded in the Dirichlet and Hecke statements. The paper's later applications are not included.

The formalized result gives a uniform logarithmic exclusion region for Landau–Siegel zeros. There is one constant $c>0$ such that every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$ and every real zero $0<\beta<1$ of its $L$-function satisfy $1-\beta\ge c/\log q$.

Both character parities are included. No explicit value of $c$ is given. This excludes real zeros in $1-c/\log q<\beta<1$, but does not rule out real zeros elsewhere in $(0,1)$.

riemann-hypothesis.doubts: (1) The Sept 30 TeX is about 16,700 lines. I read the statements, the proof overview, the Part I/II transition, the final assembly and a few lemma statements, not the body. The argument is a contradiction (assume β* > 7/8) that depends on many declared hypotheses, some of which the text says are 'verified' later. Near line 5648 the text calls the high identity 'a hypothesis to be proved for the physical expression, not its definition'; I did not trace where that is discharged. (2) Oct 5 calls its outline a sketch that suppresses coprimality conditions, local factors and smoothing; the full argument is in later sections. I read the reduction and the proof of Proposition thm:ms, which reduces to Proposition 'canonical' and the iteration, but not the reflection, transfer or appendix sections. (3) The Oct 5 README says 'This paper was written with human assistance.' The Sept 30 and Oct 1 READMEs say no such thing.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is stated. Some steps are taken from published work without proof here: the number-field quadratic large sieve of Goldmakher and Louvel, the cubic theta coefficient and transformation formulas of Patterson and Dunn–Radziwiłł, Heath-Brown's admissible-exponent method, and the Hecke functional equation. Sept 30's Part II depends on its own Part I, which it uses to get β* ≤ 11/12 and hence Δ ≤ 1/24. Oct 5 does not depend on Sept 30; its introduction cites Sept 30 only for the stronger 7/8 result.
riemann-hypothesis.direction: proves a zero-free half-plane (partial result toward RH, the quasi-RH)

grand-riemann-hypothesis.what_happened: The two zero-free-region manuscripts treat only finite-order Hecke characters of F = Q(√-3), that is, Hecke characters of trivial infinite type (GL(1) over F), together with the Dirichlet L-functions obtained from them by the transfer (GL(1) over Q). 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) claims that these have no zeros with Re s > 7/8; 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) claims no zeros with Re s > 11/12. The manuscripts do not treat infinite-type Hecke characters, GL(n) for n ≥ 2, or any other automorphic L-functions.
grand-riemann-hypothesis.delivers: Zero-free half-planes (Re s > 7/8 by Sept 30, Re s > 11/12 by Oct 5) for finite-order Hecke L-functions of Q(√-3) and for all Dirichlet L-functions. Nothing for other automorphic L-functions, and nothing on the location of zeros with Re s ≤ 7/8, so the bullet's claim is not decided.
grand-riemann-hypothesis.remains: All other automorphic L-functions (GL(n) for n ≥ 2, infinite-type Hecke L-functions over any number field, and so on), and the location claim Re ρ = 1/2 for every nontrivial zero of every automorphic L-function.

do-siegel-zeros-exist.what_happened: 'Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros' (Oct 1 2026) claims an absolute c > 0 such that every real zero β in (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3 satisfies (1−β) log q ≥ c. So no such zero lies in (1 − c/log q, 1). The paper calls this its logarithmic formulation of the Landau–Siegel zero problem. The proof is a contradiction argument: a sequence of real zeros with (1−β) log q → 0 is assumed; a prime-bias bound from the logarithmic derivative of the Hadamard product forces primes with χ(p) = −1 to carry logarithmic mass; an interpolation determinant in the biquadratic field Q(√d, √2) is divisible by many primes through the Frobenius relation, but its norm is bounded above; the comparison gives 1 ≤ 7/8. Two zero-free-half-plane manuscripts also bear on the question. 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (Oct 5 2026) says its theorem 'rules out the existence of Landau–Siegel zeros', and it excludes real zeros of all Dirichlet L-functions in (11/12, 1). 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane Re s>7/8' (Sept 30 2026) excludes them in (7/8, 1). Either fixed-window claim, if correct, gives the log-scale exclusion with δ = (log 3)/8, since |D| ≥ 3 for nonprincipal real characters.
do-siegel-zeros-exist.delivers: For fundamental discriminants D ≠ 1 (primitive nonprincipal real characters χ_D of conductor q = |D| ≥ 3) there is one absolute δ > 0, namely δ = c with c not computed, such that L(σ, χ_D) has no zero for 1 − δ/log|D| < σ < 1. So the 'is there δ > 0' form has answer yes, and the claim is that Siegel zeros, defined by this log-scale window, do not exist. The frozen wording does not define 'Siegel zero', and the paper's own statement is the log-scale one; the match depends on that definition. The text does not claim the frozen wording as literally stated.
do-siegel-zeros-exist.remains: Under the Oct 1 theorem alone: real zeros at distance at least c/log q from 1, which it does not exclude; the value of c; non-real characters; and the trivial character D = 1 (ζ), which is outside the theorem. Under the fixed-window claims, the real zeros in (0, 7/8] (Sept 30) or (0, 11/12] (Oct 5).

for-which-number-fields-does-hilberts-te.what_happened: Manuscript 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers' (main.tex, dated October 6, 2026) claims Theorem thm:main: no algorithm, given f in Z[X_1,...,X_n] with n part of the input, decides whether f has a zero in Q^n. The proof builds, for nonconstant f, a computable sequence of finite rational-solvability tests such that f has an integer zero if and only if every test succeeds. Its ingredients are a rank-one elliptic curve over F = Q(sqrt 2) supplying integer indices (Proposition ell:rank), a five-point height estimate (Theorem hei:height), a pole-parity positive existential formula obtained from two-descent (Proposition par:pole-parity), and prime-pattern lemmas. Corollary thm:degree-normal-form adds that the rational problem has Turing degree 0', and that the same holds for integer polynomials of total degree at most four and for sums of squares of degree at most two, with no bound on the number of variables. The other manuscript, 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion', is not about Hilbert's tenth problem; the Hilbert manuscript cites its Theorem 1.1 as an input (see conditional_on).
for-which-number-fields-does-hilberts-te.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-September-24-2026, A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-September-24-2026
for-which-number-fields-does-hilberts-te.delivers: Settles the case K = Q, negatively: solvability over Q of integer polynomials is undecidable, with the number of variables part of the input. Field reading (K is the field the unknowns range over): K = Q is the open rational case, and this is the one case of the bullet the manuscript decides. Ring reading (solvability in the ring of integers O_K): K = Q is Matiyasevich's 1970 theorem, so nothing new there. The manuscripts make no claim about any other number field K, either as a field or through its ring of integers. The proof is over Q; Q(sqrt 2) appears only as an auxiliary field for the elliptic curve. The introduction cites results for other K (Koymans and Pagano 2026, and Alpoge, Bhargava, Ho and Shnidman 2026, for the ring of integers of every number field; Poonen; Mazur and Rubin, conditionally) as background, not as claims of this family. So the manuscripts do not identify a class of number fields, and do not claim to answer the bullet as worded.
for-which-number-fields-does-hilberts-te.remains: Field reading: for every number field K other than Q, whether solvability over K itself is undecidable; the manuscripts neither say which K are undecidable nor say that their method extends. Ring reading: for every K other than Q, nothing in these manuscripts. The manuscripts also state that their restricted corollaries are Turing-equivalent results, not many-one completeness, and that the construction gives no single existential definition of Z in Q.
for-which-number-fields-does-hilberts-te.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched and contains no hedge about the main theorem. The abstract and Theorem thm:main agree. The main limits are the ones the text itself states: the restricted corollaries are Turing-degree statements only, and the construction gives no bound on the number of variables and no single existential definition of Z in Q. The argument is written in an elementary-extension and compactness style, with transfer principles used in the key divisibility and height steps. Its dependence on the 2-converse manuscript and on the Fontaine-Mazur preprint is as described above. I checked the statements and the main assembly, not every proof step.; conditional on: (i) The pole-parity step (Section 03, Lemma par:global-point) uses Theorem 1.1 of the pointwise 2-converse manuscript to get finiteness of Sha(E_l/Q) for curves E_l with full rational two-torsion and 2^infinity-Selmer corank at most one. The Cassels-Tate pairing argument is written out in the text. (ii) The modularity step of the height estimate (Section 04) uses the odd regular Fontaine-Mazur theorem at 2, cited as Theorem 1.1 of the OpenAI preprint 'Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2' (October 6, 2026). That preprint is outside this family and I did not read it; the text states that its hypotheses are verified for the representation at hand. (iii) The prime-pattern lemma (Section 06) uses the Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem, cited with a 2024 erratum that the text says leaves the stated inverse theorem unchanged. (iv) Other cited published results include Faltings, Bost, Zarhin, von Kaenel and Kret, Silverman, and Davis-Putnam-Robinson-Matiyasevich.

are-gamma-the-euler-mascheroni-constant-.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Catalan's constant is irrational' (OpenAI, dated 24 September 2026), proves its main theorem: Catalan's constant G = β(2) = Σ_{j≥0} (−1)^j/(2j+1)² is irrational. The proof is by contradiction. Assuming G rational, the authors form, for each N, a determinant Δ_N of size n = 48N. Its entries are integrals of explicit polynomial rows against two kernels, and each entry is a rational combination of 1, G and ζ(2). The rows have Taylor contact that cancels the ζ(2) term, so every Δ_N is rational. Three estimates are then compared. (i) A finite-place lower bound from the odd primes and the prime 2: along any sequence of N with Δ_N ≠ 0, liminf of (log|Δ_N|/n² − ½ log 2) is greater than −2.29084 (Proposition finite-lower). (ii) A nonvanishing result: for every sufficiently large prime p, v_p(Δ_p) = −96p, so Δ_p ≠ 0 (Proposition nonvanishing). This is reduced to three fixed 48×48 rational matrices, shown invertible by a mod-101 pivot certificate. (iii) A real-place upper bound: limsup over all N of the same normalized logarithm is at most −2.290939875 (Proposition real-upper), from an energy reduction with explicit trial coefficients and a rational root-count certificate. Along the prime sequence in (ii), (i) and (iii) give incompatible inequalities, so G is irrational. The conclusion adds corollaries: the minimum volume of an orientable two-cusped finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold (4G, by Agol) is irrational, as are certain arithmetic hyperbolic volumes over Q(i), which are positive rational multiples of G.
are-gamma-the-euler-mascheroni-constant-.delivers: Establishes that Catalan's constant is irrational, so G is not rational. This excludes the 'rational' answer for G in the list's trichotomy and nothing more. It does not decide whether G is algebraic irrational or transcendental, and it gives no irrationality measure. The manuscript's title, abstract and Theorem match the list's question only in the rationality part for this one number. The manuscript does not claim to settle the problem as the list states it. Its own introduction calls the result qualitative: a bound for an irrationality measure would need additional control of rational approximations. Its claims about the two hyperbolic-volume corollaries are not part of the list's question.
are-gamma-the-euler-mascheroni-constant-.remains: If the claim is correct, still open for G: whether G is algebraic irrational or transcendental, and its irrationality measure. The manuscript explicitly gives no measure. The introduction cites Viola's exponent 0.6293… and Eskandari's bound |G − p_m/q_m| ≤ q_m^(−0.62) as bounds for particular constructions, and says these are not irrationality measures. For the other thirteen numbers in the list (γ, π±e, πe, π/e, π^e, π^√2, π^π, e^(π²), ln π, 2^e, e^e, and Khinchin's constant), neither their classification nor their irrationality measures are addressed by these manuscripts.

machine_checked.scope: The formalization proves that Catalan's constant $G=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2$ is irrational. This is the mathematical assertion in the paper's title.

are-gamma-the-euler-mascheroni-constant-.doubts: (1) The real-place bound (Proposition real-upper) and the nonvanishing step (Proposition nonvanishing) are certified by computation. The real-place certificate uses rational coefficient tables scaled by 10⁻⁸, exact root brackets and derivative bounds, and rounding margins such as +0.000024 per supremum. The nonvanishing step uses a mod-101 pivot table for three 48×48 matrices whose entries are given by formulas and not printed. The text says 'supplementary programs reproduce them'. Those programs are not among the files I read. (2) The contradiction rests on a narrow margin: the finite-place bound gives greater than −2.29084 and the real-place bound gives at most −2.290939875, a gap of about 10⁻⁴ in the normalized logarithm. Both constants come from long explicit calculations with decimal rounding (for example log 2 < 0.693149). (3) Several steps are justified in a sentence or two rather than in full. For example, the 2-adic valuation bound 'follows, for example, by subtracting the factorial-floor formulas', and the energy reduction is cited to Garoufalidis–Popescu Lemma 3.1 'and its proof'. I read these at statement level and did not check them. (4) The conclusion's corollary for every orientable arithmetic hyperbolic three-orbifold over Q(i) is stated more generally than the main theorem and depends on the structure theorem cited above. (5) The abstract and main theorem agree. The introduction disclaims an irrationality measure.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed for the main theorem beyond the contradiction hypothesis G ∈ Q, which the argument refutes. It relies on cited classical results: the prime number theorem (cited to Zagier's account of Newman's proof), a Chebyshev expansion lemma from Garoufalidis–Popescu, Andréief's identity, Cauchy's double alternant, and Sarason's kernel viewpoint. It also relies on explicit computations that the text reports as certificates. It states that it does not use the result of Sun's preprint. The hyperbolic-volume corollaries in the conclusion further depend on cited results: Agol's identification of the two-cusped minimum volume (Agol 2010, Theorem 3.6), Voight's quaternion volume formula (Theorem 39.1.13), and a commensurability statement cited to Voight's Definition 38.3.4.
are-gamma-the-euler-mascheroni-constant-.direction: proves irrationality (qualitative; rules out 'rational' for G)

fontaine-mazur-conjecture.what_happened: Three manuscripts in the family; two bear directly on this problem. (a) “Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2” (FM2) claims in Theorem 1.1 that every continuous, irreducible, odd two-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ, unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, is isomorphic to a Tate twist of the 2-adic representation of a classical cuspidal eigenform. Its abstract says this resolves the odd, regular two-dimensional Fontaine–Mazur conjecture over ℚ at 2, including all residual representations. The argument has three stages: potential pro-modularity over a solvable totally real field F of even degree, split completely at 2, obtained by connectedness and patching from a modular seed (Theorem thm:potential-promodularity); production of a locally algebraic vector with the target eigensystem, using ordinary families and Thorne's Theorem D in the reducible local case and the local Langlands correspondence in the absolutely irreducible local case; and descent from a regular algebraic Hilbert cusp form over F, obtained by Jacquet–Langlands from a definite quaternion algebra, to ℚ by cyclic descent with a finite-character twist. The introduction adds that the geometric realization of modular representations gives the geometric-origin conclusion in this setting; the body does not argue that. (b) “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (UPM2) claims, with no de Rham or residual hypothesis, that every continuous odd absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional 2-adic representation of G_ℚ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in the full completed two-adic Hecke algebra 𝕋₂(N) at some odd level N: there is a continuous ℤ₂-algebra map λ: 𝕋₂(N) → O_E with λ(T_ℓ) = tr r(Frob_ℓ) and λ(ℓS_ℓ) = det r(Frob_ℓ). It states that it does not assert classical modularity. Its proof places r in a fixed-determinant trace family, finds an auxiliary regular de Rham point x, applies FM2's Theorem 1.1 to x to get classicality, and then uses the dimension theorem of (c) and Newton–Thorne's adjoint Selmer vanishing to show the original point lies on Hecke support (conclusion.tex, proof of Theorem main). (c) “The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level” (DHA) claims that for every odd N every irreducible component of Spec 𝕋₂(N) has Krull dimension exactly 4, the p = 2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture. It makes no claim about Galois modularity; it bears on this problem only as an input to UPM2.
fontaine-mazur-conjecture.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime-two-October-4-2026, Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-September-23-2026
fontaine-mazur-conjecture.delivers: For the list's Fontaine–Mazur problem, FM2 proves, at p = 2 only, the odd, regular, two-dimensional case over ℚ: an odd, irreducible, two-dimensional 2-adic representation, de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and unramified outside finitely many primes, is modular up to Tate twist (a classical cuspidal eigenform). The residual representation is unrestricted, and scalar and reducible residual cases are included. This corresponds to the list's part (3), restricted to dimension two, odd, regular, and at 2, and to the modularity half of part (2) in that case. The list's part (3) matches FM2's statement, apart from the prime, which is 2 only. The list's part (2) uses ‘potentially semistable at p’ and FM2 uses ‘de Rham at 2’; the text passes from de Rham to potentially semistable by citing Berger (lemma dense-Thorne-points). The geometric-origin conclusion of part (1) is asserted in one sentence of the introduction and not proved in the body. FM2's introduction says that, together with odd-prime results discussed there (Pan 2022; Zhang 2025 for p = 3), the theorem gives the modularity conclusion ‘at every prime’. Those odd-prime results are other papers, and this family proves only p = 2. UPM2 delivers less: occurrence in a completed Hecke algebra for every odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation, with no Hodge–Tate or de Rham condition. It delivers no classical modularity for any representation, so it does not give the conjecture's conclusion. DHA delivers no Galois-theoretic conclusion. The manuscripts claim to resolve the odd regular two-dimensional case over ℚ at 2, not the conjecture as a whole. None of them addresses the even case, the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight case, totally real base fields, the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement, the group-theoretic reading, or the tame variant.
fontaine-mazur-conjecture.remains: If the claims hold, the following stay open for the list's problem: (i) every prime other than 2 within this family, since the every-prime statement depends on external odd-prime papers; (ii) the even two-dimensional case, where the conjecture predicts nonexistence; (iii) the equal-Hodge–Tate-weight (irregular) case for classical modularity, where UPM2 gives only occurrence; (iv) general dimension, general number fields, and the geometric-origin conclusion beyond the one-sentence claim; (v) totally real base fields (list item 6); (vi) the unramified-everywhere / finite-image statement (item 7), the group-theoretic reading (item 8), and the tame variant (item 9); (vii) classical modularity of the representations that UPM2 shows occur in the completed Hecke algebra, which UPM2 says it does not assert.
fontaine-mazur-conjecture.doubts: FM2: (1) The geometric-origin conclusion is asserted in a single sentence of the introduction with no argument in the body, which ends at ‘classical cuspidal eigenform’. (2) The reducible local branch rests on Thorne's 2026 preprint (Theorem D), which is cited as the source of modularity for its dense ordinary points. (3) The every-prime claim in the introduction depends on odd-prime results outside the family. (4) The virtually solvable case (Lemma solvable-reduction) is argued in about sixty lines: the imaginary quadratic subcase is handled by citing theta series and Jacquet–Langlands, and the real quadratic subcase by a unit-theorem argument. (5) I read the statements and key steps of the classicality, connectedness and preliminaries sections; I did not read the patching, deformation, completed_forms or fields sections in full, and checked them only by grep for hedging language. I did not check the proofs in detail. UPM2: (1) Its main theorem is occurrence, not classicality, so it inherits every dependency on FM2 and DHA. (2) Thorne's Theorem D is named in the introduction as an essential input, but I found no body section citing it. (3) The marked-line, transverse-chart and Selmer-loss construction for the scalar and reducible-residue branches is described in the introduction; I read the introduction and the regular-point section (lines 1–60, 330–404) in full and grepped family.tex, diagonal.tex and hecke.tex for citations and hedging words only, so those branches are checked only at the level of the introduction. DHA: (1) The lower bound (every component has dimension at least 4) is quoted from Emerton's Corollary 2.28 ‘with p = 2’. The text says its own determinant argument supplies the p = 2 justification for Emerton's Theorem 2.7, which had an odd-prime restriction; whether that repair also covers Corollary 2.28 is asserted, not separately shown. (2) The Selmer-vanishing input, Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 specialised to GL₂/ℚ, is stated to include p = 2 and a CM condition. The cited paper's title, ‘Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type’, is about unitary-type groups, so the specialisation carries real weight in the argument.; conditional on: FM2's Theorem 1.1 relies on cited results it does not prove. Thorne, ‘Towards the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture for GL₂’ (arXiv:2608.07186v1, a 2026 preprint), Theorem D, is used in the reducible local branch to make dense ordinary points modular (lemma dense-Thorne-points); this is the main external dependency. Other inputs are BLGGT 2014 Theorem 2.1.1 (Galois representations for Hilbert cusp forms at 2), Colmez 2010 and Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas 2014 (local p-adic Langlands at 2), Berger 2002 (de Rham implies potentially semistable), Jacquet–Langlands and Arthur–Clozel (base change and descent), and Billerey–Menares 2016 for the existence of cuspidal lifts in the reducible-residue connectedness step, which the manuscript says it re-proves in detail. UPM2 is conditional on FM2 (Theorem 1.1 applied to its auxiliary point, and the curve and connectedness arguments it takes from FM2), on DHA (its dimension-four theorem), on Newton–Thorne 2023 Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ, and on Allen 2016 Lemma 1.1.3. Its introduction also cites Thorne's Theorem D as supplying an essential set of classical points, but I found no body section that cites Thorne. DHA is conditional on Emerton's Corollary 2.28 (the lower bound of dimension 4) and on Newton–Thorne Theorem 5.4 as specialised to GL₂/ℚ at p = 2.
fontaine-mazur-conjecture.direction: proves a case: odd, regular, two-dimensional over ℚ at p = 2, classical modularity up to Tate twist; plus a weaker occurrence-only pro-modularity result for all odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional cases at 2

ramanujan-petersson-conjecture.what_happened: Three manuscripts make temperedness claims, all over function fields F = F_q(X). (1) Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level, Corollary 1.2: for split connected adjoint absolutely simple G, a cuspidal automorphic representation with one generic unramified local component is tempered at every unramified place. The proof forces the orbit label at the good places to be zero, using the local criterion of Ciubotaru-Harris (their Corollary 6.32(1)), and the paper says the common orbit removes the tempered-place hypothesis of their Theorem 5.4. (2) Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups, Theorem 1: for split connected adjoint absolutely simple G of type G2, F4, E6, E7 or E8, every local component of a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A_F) is tempered at every place, ramified places included, with no restriction on characteristic or ramification depth. It takes the unramified places from (1) and reaches the ramified places through a pure-completion local criterion (Theorem thm:local-criterion). (3) Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters gives no temperedness conclusion. It produces an SL_2 factor and a centralizer part of weight zero, so Frobenius eigenvalues have absolute value one only on the centralizer part, not in general. Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration, The Restricted Geometric Langlands Equivalence in Positive Characteristic, and the three tame Hecke eigensheaf manuscripts do not bear on temperedness.
ramanujan-petersson-conjecture.delivers: Function fields only, and only for generic cuspidal representations. The two temperedness results have different scopes. Temperedness paper: globally generic cuspidal representations, exceptional split adjoint absolutely simple G, all places. Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2: one generic unramified local component suffices, any split adjoint absolutely simple G (this includes PGL_n), unramified places only. The abstract of the Temperedness paper says it proves the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for the globally generic exceptional case; that is the scope of the claim, not the conjecture in full. For GL_n over function fields the family adds nothing new: the Temperedness introduction records that Laurent Lafforgue proved Ramanujan for GL_n. Not covered: the holomorphic Petersson bound (part a) and the Maass-form statement (part b), which concern number fields such as Q; no manuscript in the family addresses them. Also not covered: non-generic cuspidal representations.
ramanujan-petersson-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct: temperedness for non-generic cuspidal representations, which the Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition places into orbit summands but does not bound; unramified places for cuspidal representations with no generic unramified local component; ramified places for split adjoint absolutely simple groups outside the five exceptional types, since the headline theorem does not state them (see doubts); number fields and parts (a) and (b); non-adjoint and non-split groups.
ramanujan-petersson-conjecture.doubts: (i) The headline theorem is limited to G2, F4, E6, E7 and E8, but the local criterion (Theorem thm:local-criterion) and the global argument in sections/global.tex are stated for any split adjoint absolutely simple group, and the introduction says generic Ramanujan for split classical groups was already proved by Lomeli. The text gives no reason for the exceptional restriction, and I did not find a step in the parts I read that uses exceptionality. (ii) The removal of Ciubotaru-Harris's tempered-place hypothesis in Corollary 1.2 is asserted in the text and rests on applying their Corollary 6.32(1); I did not check that application. (iii) Corollary 1.2 rests on the local decomposition theorem (Theorem ext:discrete, in the sections on the local geometry), which I did not read. A search of these manuscripts for sketch-type hedges found none in the parts that bear on temperedness.; conditional on: The Temperedness paper's unramified step is Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2, which relies on the Ciubotaru-Harris local criterion (their Corollary 6.32(1)), an external result not proved in the family. The Temperedness paper also takes these as cited inputs: Lafforgue and Genestier-Lafforgue parameters and local-global compatibility (Theorem thm:parameters); the Gan-Harris-Sawin tempered completion (Theorem thm:tempered-completion); the Gan-Lomeli globalization theorem and Lomeli's crude functional equation for the local-coefficient comparison; and Deligne's theorem on weights of local monodromy (Weil II, 1.8.4). The Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2 also uses V. Lafforgue's global parameter theorem.
ramanujan-petersson-conjecture.direction: proves a case: generic cuspidal representations are tempered (all places for exceptional adjoint groups; unramified places for split adjoint absolutely simple groups from one generic unramified component)
