arthurs-conjectures.what_happened: Four manuscripts engage Arthur's conjectures. None proves a packet-level statement. (1) Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters: assuming the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (its Theorem 1.1, cited as Parent), for each occurring excursion character nu of a split connected semisimple group over a global function field, at any full finite level, it constructs an algebraic SL_2 homomorphism phi_nu into the dual group, whose differential sends the raising element into the nilpotent orbit O_nu given by the decomposition, and a continuous homomorphism tau_nu from the Weil group W_U into the algebraic centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), with reductive Zariski closure and eigenvalues of absolute value one at every complex embedding, such that after one fixed conjugation sigma_nu(w) = tau_nu(w) phi_nu(diag(a^deg(w), a^-deg(w))) for all w in W_U, inertia included. (2) Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level, unconditionally: for split semisimple G over a global function field, the cuspidal function space at any full finite level, with arbitrary divisor multiplicities, splits as a direct sum over nilpotent orbits of the dual group, both rationally and over Q-bar_ell. At level zero this proves Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. (3) Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration: for split connected semisimple G, under four characteristic conditions, the canonical filtration on finitely supported unramified automorphic functions is defined over Q for every closed invariant nilpotent support. The paper presents this as Conjecture 2.7.3 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. Its cuspidal corollary identifies the level-zero cuspidal part with the rational orbit summands of (2), which the paper calls the common-scope form of Conjectures 3.4.9 and 3.4.11. (4) The Temperedness paper and Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2 give only generic-case temperedness, which the problem's lead names as a consequence of Arthur's conjectures; see the ramanujan-petersson-conjecture entry. The Restricted Geometric Langlands full-support manuscript and the three tame Hecke eigensheaf manuscripts do not bear on Arthur's conjectures. They concern geometric Langlands support and eigensheaves with tame unipotent monodromy, and make no claim about Arthur parameters, packets or SL_2 factors.
arthurs-conjectures.delivers: Each of (1)-(3) is a Galois-side or spectral-support structure over function fields for split groups: a commuting SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair recovering each occurring excursion parameter, an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration. None states or proves the global Arthur packet decomposition of the discrete spectrum, local Arthur packets, unitarity of packet members, or the multiplicity formula. The Global Arthur paper says explicitly that it asserts no ellipticity, no Arthur-packet classification and no multiplicity formula. No manuscript claims to settle Arthur's conjectures. The family's result is function-field and split-group only, so the number-field content of the problem's lead is outside it. The text frames the commuting pair as the parameter-level part of V. Lafforgue's Arthur conjecture, whose elliptic form it does not prove. Whether the Galois-side pair counts as an Arthur-type parameter for the statement is for the judging pass to decide.
arthurs-conjectures.remains: If the claims are correct, the parts of the problem's list not covered are still open as far as this family goes: global and local Arthur packets and their character identities, Arthur's multiplicity formula, unitarity of packet members, the 1989 unipotent conjectures, and ellipticity of the global parameter (V. Lafforgue's version, not claimed here). For the generalized Ramanujan part, the family gives generic-case temperedness only. Also open: the enhancement is existential, with no uniqueness or multiplicity statement, and no link to packets is made.
arthurs-conjectures.doubts: (i) thm:parent in the Global Arthur paper is stated for occurring excursion characters, but the decomposition it cites (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper) is stated for joint eigencharacters of spherical Hecke operators at good places. The passage between the two is asserted with a citation; I did not verify it. (ii) The Global Arthur proof is a contradiction argument of about 5,400 lines. I did not read the lemmas it depends on, such as lem:tensor-nilpotence, prop:ind-qc-comparison and prop:open-orbit-enhancement. (iii) The Rationality paper flags a scope caveat itself: its pure Weil lift input (Theorem inp:pure-lift) is cited to a proposition stated for irreducible Weil parameters, and the paper uses a semisimple consequence recorded in a GLR appendix. A search of these manuscripts for sketch-type hedges found none in the parts that bear on Arthur's conjectures.; conditional on: Global Arthur Enhancements assumes the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper, restated there as thm:parent) and uses further results of that paper, cited as Parent: Sections 2-3, Lemma 6.4, Theorems 2.2-2.3, Propositions 2.5-2.7 and Lemma 3.6. It also cites external inputs: Xue's finiteness and smoothness theorems for stacks of shtukas, the nearby-cycle comparisons of Salmon and Eteve-Xue, Laurent Lafforgue's purity theorem, and Bezrukavnikov and Ben-Zvi-Chen-Helm-Nadler for the local coherent models. Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration assumes the four characteristic conditions of restricted geometric Langlands theory and uses the restricted equivalence and trace inputs of AGKRRV, Gaitsgory-Raskin and Raskin as cited. Its cuspidal corollary depends on the Ramanujan-Arthur paper (Theorem 1.1, Lemmas 6.1-6.2, Propositions 6.5-6.6, Remark 6.3).
arthurs-conjectures.direction: constructs Galois-side Arthur-type data over function fields (an SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair per occurring excursion parameter), proves an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and proves rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration; no packets
arthurs-conjectures.object: phi_nu: SL_2 into the dual group and tau_nu: W_U into the centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), attached to each occurring excursion character. Constructed by an existence argument (the proof of Theorem thm:main proceeds by contradiction); not explicit.

zilber-pink-conjecture.what_happened: Four manuscripts, all stated over Q̄. (1) 'The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture' claims that for every abelian variety A over a number field K and every irreducible subvariety X ⊆ A over Q̄, X has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties. Atypicality is measured in S = ⟨X⟩_sp, the smallest torsion coset containing X: an irreducible Y is atypical if it is a component of X ∩ T for a torsion coset T ⊆ S with dim Y > dim X + dim T − dim S. The text also gives an equivalent form: finitely many proper atypical Y₁,…,Y_m such that every atypical subvariety lies in one of them. The route is a non-density theorem (if X lies in no proper torsion coset, X ∩ A^[dim X+1] is not Zariski dense in X, where A^[r] is the union of torsion cosets of codimension ≥ r), proved via an auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8), and then a reduction to maximal-atypical finiteness using Barroero–Dill Thm 1.9 and Habegger–Pila Thm 9.8 (§9). A finite-rank translated-intersection corollary is also stated. (2) 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points s whose abelian surface is isogenous to E₁×E₂ with at least one factor CM (isogenies need not respect the polarization; the both-CM case is included). Its new input is a Galois-orbit lower bound for 'mixed' points (one CM, one non-CM factor): orbit size ≥ c·max{N(s), |disc End(F)|}^(1/42), where N(s) is the minimal degree of a product isogeny; the constant depends on C and K and is ineffective. Finiteness then follows from Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, as corrected) and, for the both-CM and special points, Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). (3) 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' claims that a reduced irreducible Hodge-generic closed curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose full geometric endomorphism algebra is an indefinite quaternion division algebra over ℚ. It proves a height bound h(t) ≤ c[K(t):K]^c′ for such points (Thm thm:height), via a common-relation interpolation theorem (§2) and Frobenius cross-pairings in a rank-five quadratic variation, then a counting argument: the period image would lie in a subset of the isotropic quadric of dimension ≤ 2, whereas full monodromy makes it Zariski dense. (4) 'Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' claims that a Hodge-generic curve C ⊂ A₂ over Q̄ has only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to E² with E non-CM. It proves a Galois-orbit bound for these points in terms of the discriminant of the full endomorphism order and applies Daw–Orr's conditional counting theorem in its E² case, the orbit bound supplying its hypothesis. It then states the full curve case: for Hodge-generic C over Q̄, only finitely many points of C lie on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1 (this combines (4) with the companion theorems (2) and (3)), plus a special-closure corollary for every curve over Q̄.
zilber-pink-conjecture.delivers: Does not settle the frozen problem, which is stated over C and covers mixed Shimura and semiabelian varieties in general. What is claimed, all over Q̄ only: (a) Abelian varieties (ambient class (2), abelian case): for every abelian variety over Q̄ and every irreducible subvariety, finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties, with atypicality relative to the smallest containing torsion coset. That is the 'maximal' reading. The literal frozen reading ('finitely many atypical subvarieties') is not what is proved: the manuscript gives finitely many maximal ones and says every atypical subvariety lies in one of them, but makes no finiteness claim for the set of all atypical subvarieties. (b) A₂ (a pure Shimura variety, ambient class (1)), curves only: for Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, finitely many points on special subvarieties of dimension ≤ 1, which is the full curve case (Thm intro:zp in (4)). For a Hodge-generic curve in A₂ the atypical subvarieties are points (a special surface meets it only in points, which are not atypical there), so the 'all' and 'maximal' readings coincide in that case. That is my reading of the definition, not a statement in the manuscripts. For non-Hodge-generic curves over Q̄, the special-closure corollary gives the analogous finiteness, with codimension taken inside the smallest special S_C containing the curve. (c) Quantifier (3): all subvarieties of abelian varieties over Q̄; only curves in A₂. (d) Atypicality convention: the manuscripts take codimension inside the smallest special subvariety containing X. The frozen list does not say which ambient S it means, so the judge should check that choice. The manuscripts do not claim to resolve the conjecture as stated.
zilber-pink-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct, still open: (a) the statement over C, and any X not defined over Q̄; (b) semiabelian varieties with nontrivial torus part (algebraic tori, general semiabelian varieties); (c) mixed Shimura varieties other than A₂ (Kuga type, other pure Shimura varieties); (d) for abelian varieties, finiteness of all atypical subvarieties rather than only the maximal ones; (e) subvarieties of A₂ of dimension ≥ 2; (f) effective or uniform bounds, none of which are claimed (the orbit and finiteness constants are ineffective).
zilber-pink-conjecture.doubts: (a) The abelian abstract calls its Q̄-restricted maximal-atypical statement 'the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture'. The restriction to number fields appears in the theorem statement but not in the abstract's second sentence. (b) I did not check the proof of the auxiliary sequence theorem (§§2–8) line by line; the sections I read show no hedges. (c) E×CM: the Daw–Orr input is cited to the corrected arXiv v4 (2021), not the published text, and the footnote attributes the reduction-theory correction to Orr–Schnell. (d) E×CM: some steps are argued by citation rather than computed. The chart computation in Lemma boundary-comparison ends by invoking 'the fixed rational factor' and 'the fixed level datum'. Lemma family-height says an omitted finite set 'can be included by enlarging the constant'. (e) E×CM: the effective remark rests on a zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions, cited to another OpenAI preprint. That is a very strong input, but the main theorems do not use it. (f) Quaternionic: the counting step (Prop counting-finiteness) is compressed. It says the arc has Nash coordinates 'algebraic over its real parameter' with 'transcendence degree at most one', and the quoted Habegger–Pila corollary is not restated in the section. (g) Elliptic squares: the interpolation theorem is titled 'Conditional height bound'. Its hypothesis (iv) is discharged in §07 (Prop nid:nonidentity), so the E² result depends on §07 being correct. (h) Elliptic squares: the paper calls its use of Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 'the precise E² case of the published conditional finiteness theorem'. The hypotheses in §§6.5–6.6 of Daw–Orr are cited, not restated, so the match is not checked here.; conditional on: (1) Abelian paper: no unproven hypothesis is assumed; it relies on published results only (Barroero–Dill 2021 Thm 1.9, Habegger–Pila 2016 Thm 9.8, Ax's analytic-subgroup theorem and others) and on no other family manuscript. (2) E×CM: relies on Daw–Orr's implication (their Thm 1.2, taken from the corrected arXiv v4 rather than the published 2021 text, with the reduction-theory correction of Orr–Schnell), on Siegel's class-number bound (ineffective), and on Andre–Oort for A₂ (Pila–Tsimerman). Its effective-constant remark (rem:effective-cm) uses another OpenAI manuscript, the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis zero-free half-plane preprint (OAI:The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026). That manuscript is not in this family and I did not read it; the main theorems do not use the remark. (3) Quaternionic paper: no unproven hypothesis that I could identify; relies on Habegger–Pila Cor. 7.2 (quoted with k=1), Pila–Wilkie and Pila's counting results, Andre's monodromy theorem, and its own interpolation theorem (§2; I read only the statement). (4) Elliptic-squares paper: the E² theorem rests on Daw–Orr Thm 1.3 with their Conjecture 6.2, which the paper verifies for the E² locus only; it also uses Masser–Wüstholz endomorphism estimates and Andre's normality theorem. The full curve theorem (Thm intro:zp) and its special-closure corollary depend on two other family manuscripts: 'The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A₂' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (2) here) and 'Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold' (its Thm 1.1, which is item (3) here).
zilber-pink-conjecture.direction: proves a case: abelian varieties over Q̄ (maximal-atypical form), and curves in A₂ over Q̄ (Hodge-generic and special-closure)

flint-hills-series.what_happened: The single manuscript, 'The irrationality exponent of pi is 2' (build/main.tex), claims two results. (1) Theorem 1.1 (thm:main): for every real ν>2 there is an integer Q(ν) such that |π − p/q| ≥ q^(−ν) for all integers p and all integers q ≥ Q(ν); fractions need not be reduced. With the pigeonhole bound μ(π) ≥ 2 this gives μ(π) = 2. (2) Corollary 1.2 (thm:flinthills): the classical Flint–Hills series Σ_{n≥1} 1/(n³ sin²n), angles in radians, converges. The corollary is proved in sections/series.tex. Fix ν in (2, 5/2); Theorem 1.1 gives ‖qπ‖ ≥ c·q^(1−ν) for all q ≥ 1, with c > 0 absorbing the finitely many q below Q. A dyadic spacing lemma (series:dyadic) turns this into Σ 1/(q³‖qπ‖²) < ∞. Each n is grouped by its nearest multiple q of π, and each group's contribution is bounded by (8/π)/(q³‖qπ‖²). The proof does not use the cited Alekseyev (μ ≤ 5/2 is necessary) or Meiburg (μ < 5/2 is sufficient) results. The same manuscript also states Corollary (series:generalized): for fixed a, b > 0, Σ 1/(n^a |sin n|^b) with angles in radians converges if and only if a > max{1, b}. The abstract and introduction present both results as proved.
flint-hills-series.delivers: Convergence of the classical Flint–Hills series 1/(n³ sin²n), angles in radians: the manuscript claims the answer to the question is yes. Its framing matches the problem_asks reading. The introduction states the problem as whether Σ 1/(n³ sin²n) converges with angles in radians, and the claim answers that question affirmatively. The only hypothesis is the manuscript's own Theorem 1.1. That theorem's threshold Q(ν) is ineffective, but convergence needs only existence. The generalized criterion (a > max{1, b}) goes beyond the problem's single series.
flint-hills-series.remains: Nothing that problem_asks requires. The bullet asks only whether the series converges. The manuscript gives no value of the sum, no rate of the tail, and no explicit threshold Q(ν).

machine_checked.scope:
The formalization proves that the irrationality exponent of $\pi$ is exactly two. For every $\nu>2$, all sufficiently large positive denominators $q$ satisfy $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-\nu}$ for every integer numerator $p$. It also states the exact supremum characterization using infinitely many rational approximations.

The paper's convergence consequence for the Flint–Hills series is outside this selected statement.

flint-hills-series.doubts: No step is flagged as sketched, and the abstract, Corollary 1.2 and its proof contain no hedges. Points that bear on trust: (a) the manuscript states that the threshold Q(ν) in Theorem 1.1 is not given effectively (main.tex, lines 74–75); (b) the proof of Theorem 1.1 rests on a new separated-weight interpolation theorem (sections/interpolation.tex) that the paper proves itself rather than citing, and the outline says a dimension count alone does not establish the needed full-rank statement (main.tex, lines 183–185); the Flint–Hills claim inherits whatever holds for that argument; (c) the task's description of the repository's Lean formalisation (lean/docs/017.md) says it covers the exponent-two statement but not the Flint–Hills consequence, so by that description the convergence step is not formally covered. I did not open the Lean file.

section-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts. (1) 'The p-adic section conjecture' (OpenAI, 6 October 2026) claims the local p-adic section conjecture: for every prime p, every finite extension k/ℚ_p and every smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/k of genus at least two, the map from X(k) to the set of continuous group-homomorphic splittings s: G_k → π_1(X) of π_1(X) → G_k, modulo conjugation by the geometric fundamental group π_1(X_k̄), is bijective (Theorem 1.1, thm:section). Surjectivity (Section 7) is argued as follows. A completion theorem (Theorem thm:completion, proved in Section 6 from patching in Section 3, collar roots in Sections 4 and 5, and cited inputs from Mochizuki–Tsujimura, Amini–Baker–Brugallé–Rabinoff and Raynaud / Bosch–Lütkebohmert) places the separable closure of k(X) inside the completion of the universal étale function field. Rank-one localisations of a section are excluded by Koenigsmann's birational section theorem and an explicit two-valuation argument (Lemma no-rank-one-section). In the remaining case the closed point has residue field k, because the section surjects onto G_k, and Pop–Stix's type-2h analysis then identifies the section with a point section. Injectivity (end of Section 7) is a Kummer-type argument on the Jacobian, using the local logarithm. The same manuscript also states a global theorem over number fields K: for a smooth proper geometrically connected C/K of genus at least two, C(K) → Sec(C/K) is bijective whenever the finite-cover descent locus equals C(K) (Theorem global-descent). It gives three corollaries under which that equality holds: abelian targets (Corollary global-abelian-target), an elliptic target E/ℚ with Selmer corank zero at one prime (Corollary global-selmer-target), and the modular curves X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus at least two over ℚ (Corollary global-modular-curves). (2) 'Étale covers with a prescribed exterior sheet' (OpenAI, 24 September 2026) does not bear on sections. Over k̄, for a smooth proper hyperbolic curve X and finitely many disjoint disks V_i with exterior U, it constructs a connected smooth proper Y and a finite étale surjective g: Y → X such that a component of g^{-1}(U) maps isomorphically to U and every component of g^{-1}(V_i) has degree divisible by p over V_i. It mentions no sections, rational points or Galois splittings, and the p-adic manuscript does not cite it.
section-conjecture.revisions: 1 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: The-p-adic-section-conjecture-September-24-2026
section-conjecture.delivers: Local case: for k finite over ℚ_p and genus at least two, both halves of the bijection (surjectivity and injectivity) for the full arithmetic π_1 with conjugacy by the geometric π_1, which is what the list's (a) and (b) describe. This is not the frozen quantifier: a finite extension of ℚ_p is not a finitely generated field, so the local theorem does not by itself settle the problem as frozen. Global case: for a smooth proper geometrically connected C/K of genus at least two over a number field K, κ_C is bijective under the finite-cover descent equality. The manuscript supplies that equality only for the listed cases: X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus at least two over ℚ (the abstract says 'this includes' these); abelian targets with A(K) finite and Sha(A/K)_div = 0, or a Jacobian with J(K) finite and Sha(J/K)_div = 0; and curves with a nonconstant ℚ-morphism to an elliptic curve E with s_p(E) = 0 for at least one p. The manuscript does not claim to settle the section conjecture in general. Against the list: the splitting-and-conjugacy formulation and the bijectivity match (a) and (b) on the covered curves. The quantifiers differ. The list names no genus and all finitely generated fields; the paper assumes genus at least two and characteristic zero, treats finite extensions of ℚ_p locally, and treats only number fields globally.
section-conjecture.remains: If the claim is correct, the frozen problem stays open in general. (i) Finitely generated fields other than number fields and finite extensions of ℚ_p: for example function fields of curves over number fields or finite fields, and fields of positive characteristic, since the manuscript works only in characteristic zero. (ii) For number fields, every curve whose finite-cover descent locus is not known to equal its rational points, including curves of genus at least two outside the three listed criteria. (iii) Curves of genus 0 and 1, which the genus-two hypothesis excludes (the frozen statement names no genus). (iv) Without the descent equality, the global bijection is not claimed; the manuscript says the equality 'remains a separate arithmetic hypothesis'.
section-conjecture.doubts: (1) The last step of surjectivity is delegated. The text says 'Equivalently, the type-2h conclusion of [Pop–Stix, Section 6.1] gives s = s_a', and the sentence 'For the full étale tower the horizontal inertia is trivial, and the horizontal decomposition group is the point section at a' is asserted without argument. (2) 'The valuation transcendence inequality gives ratrank(Γ_w/Γ_k) ≤ 1' is stated with no reference and no proof. (3) Injectivity compresses its key step into one sentence: conjugate sections induce isomorphic G_k-actions on the geometric fibres of [n] on J, so fixed points are preserved. The text calls this 'the usual Kummer argument'. (4) The modular-curve corollary covers 'every positive integer N such that X_0(N) has genus at least two' without listing those N, and rests entirely on Stoll's Corollary 8.8. The text says the stated equalities are 'retained' under the erratum, so the claim depends on the erratum's corrected form of a published result, which the manuscript does not reprove. (5) Several cited inputs are 'preprint version' references (Pop–Stix, Koenigsmann, Harari–Stix, Betts–Stix). I did not check those versions. (6) The README notes a previous version of this manuscript (24 September 2026) with revised citations. I did not compare the versions.; conditional on: Global results (Section 8, 'Global consequences via finite descent'): the finite-cover equality (eq. finite-cover-equality) is an assumed hypothesis. For the modular curves it is supplied by Stoll's Corollary 8.8 (Finite descent obstructions and rational points on curves), as corrected by Stoll's erratum. The abelian-target corollary uses Stoll's Corollary 8.1 and Theorem 8.6. The elliptic-target corollary uses the companion manuscript 'The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime' (OpenAI, October 2026), cited as OpenAISelmerConverse2026, Theorem 1.1, which I did not read. The surjectivity argument uses Pop–Stix's valuative localisation (Theorem 26) and their type-2h analysis (Section 6.1), and Koenigsmann's Proposition 2.4(2); all three are cited as preprint versions. The completion theorem uses Mochizuki–Tsujimura's resolution theorem, Amini–Baker–Brugallé–Rabinoff's Theorem 7.7 and Raynaud / Bosch–Lütkebohmert uniformisation. The global corollaries also use Harari–Stix's Theorem 2.1 and Stix's finite-support corollary, and the real-place step uses Bresciani–Vistoli's real section theorem. The 'Étale covers' manuscript is not used by this one.
section-conjecture.direction: proves the conjecture for finite extensions of ℚ_p (genus at least two), and proves it for listed number-field cases; no general proof

gaussian-moat-problem.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes' (dated 26 September 2026, author listed as 'OpenAI'), claims the Gaussian moat conjecture in a uniform form. Its Theorem 'Uniform component bound' (main.tex) says: for every finite real D there is a finite B_D such that every connected component of the graph G_D has at most B_D vertices. G_D has all Gaussian primes as vertices, with an edge between distinct z, w when the Euclidean distance |z - w| is at most D. The bound is independent of the starting prime and includes primes on the coordinate axes. The corollary is that every sequence of distinct Gaussian primes with successive distances at most D has at most B_D terms, so no infinite such sequence exists for any D. For D < 1 the bound B_D = 1 is immediate, since distinct lattice points are then never adjacent. The argument reduces this (periodicity.tex, Proposition 'From a periodic obstruction to a uniform bound') to a finite sieve theorem (main.tex, Theorem 'Finite sieve obstruction'; its proof is at the end of information.tex). That theorem says: for each D >= 1 there is a finite set P_D of rational primes congruent to 1 mod 4 such that the set A(P_D) of Gaussian integers avoiding both chosen conjugate prime factors of each p in P_D contains no infinite self-avoiding walk with steps at most D. The proof of the sieve theorem is a contradiction argument. If an avoiding walk exists for large M, then entropy and information estimates on prime batches (geometric sampling of endpoints, a coverage-transfer theorem, a common sampling schedule with a shared terminal-time law, and a telescoping entropy budget) force a sum of per-batch information costs, each at least c_1/log T, to be at most log K_D and yet to diverge as M grows.
gaussian-moat-problem.delivers: If the claim holds, it answers the bullet negatively for the Euclidean metric and for every step bound C: no infinite sequence of distinct Gaussian primes with |x_{n+1} - x_n| <= C exists, from any starting prime. The manuscript's abstract says 'We prove the Gaussian moat conjecture', and its introduction says the result 'proves the uniform form of the Gaussian moat conjecture and answers the infinite-walk question negatively'. Its formulation ('whether some G_D contains an infinite path with no repeated vertex') is the list's question in graph language, so the wording matches up to notation. The claim also covers the origin-started variant, since it applies to every starting prime. Beyond the bullet, it gives a uniform bound on component sizes of G_D.
gaussian-moat-problem.remains: If the claim is correct, neither part (a) nor part (b) of the bullet remains open. The manuscript does not give an explicit B_D, an explicit P_D or M, or any explicit dependence of the bound on D. The bound is stated to be nonexplicit.

machine_checked.scope: The Gaussian moat problem asks whether an infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have bounded step lengths. The formalized result gives a negative answer for every real step bound $D$. More strongly, one finite bound depending only on $D$ limits the size of every connected component of the bounded-step graph and the length of every injective bounded-step walk. Axis primes and all associates are included. No explicit function of $D$ is supplied.

gaussian-moat-problem.doubts: (a) The thresholds are not explicit. The constants g_0, c_0 and B and the threshold for M are only asserted to exist ('for sufficiently large M'), and uniformity over the hypothetical walks is asserted rather than quantified. (b) The argument relies on material I did not check in full: the choice of constants and the iteration in schedule.tex (I read lines 1-60 and 400-538 only), the entropy and displacement estimates behind the labelled equations smoothing, native-data, checkpoint-entropy and terminal-entropy, the geometric lemmas in geometry.tex (I read only the enrichment statement and its surrounding text), and the proof of Proposition 'Information cost of one batch' in information.tex (I read lines 1-60 and 280-417 only). (c) The schedule section states that conditioning on residue vectors 'will be treated separately' in the next section. I did not confirm that the information section fully discharges this. (d) The entropy-enrichment lemma is stated for an 'asymptotic family' with an O_D(g) error term and no explicit rates. (e) The text states the result without hedges. It is attributed to 'OpenAI' with no individual authors, and the references are all predecessors (Gethner-Stark, Gethner-Wagon-Wick, Tsuchimura, Vardi, Tao, Selberg, Lugosi, Conrad and Cover-Thomas).
gaussian-moat-problem.direction: proves the conjecture: no infinite bounded-step walk through Gaussian primes, in a uniform component-size form
gaussian-moat-problem.object: No explicit object. The obstruction is a finite set P_D of rational primes congruent to 1 mod 4, with a chosen Gaussian factor for each, defining a periodic set A(P_D) in Z[i]. It is not explicit: P_D is taken to be P_M for an unspecified sufficiently large M, which is found by contradiction. No infinite walk is constructed, since the result is a nonexistence claim.

artins-conjecture-on-primitive-roots.what_happened: Two manuscripts. (a) 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' claims that for every integer a that is neither -1 nor a square there are c_a > 0 and x_a >= 2 such that, for every real x >= x_a, at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) satisfy p not dividing a and ord_p(a) = p - 1 (the main theorem of the introduction; the abstract states the same). The proof (01a-reduction.tex) builds primes p = c r Q + 1 with c in {2, 4}, Q > x^0.9 prime, and every prime factor of r in (exp((log x)^0.1), exp((log x)^0.3)), inside a residue class modulo M = 8 times the odd primes dividing a, chosen so that (a/p) = -1. This makes the index (p-1)/ord_p(a) odd. Primes whose index has Q as a factor are discarded using a bound on the product of |a^j - 1| for j up to 2x^0.1. Primes whose index has a prime factor l dividing r are discarded using a uniform Kummer-splitting bound (stated in 01a-reduction.tex, proved in 07-splitting.tex), which rests on the Hecke zero-free theorem (Theorem 1.2). (b) 'Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases' proves that for any finite set of distinct positive primes q_1, ..., q_k there are at least c x/(log x)^2 primes p in (x, 2x) with p not dividing q_1...q_k and ord_p(q_i) = p - 1 for every i. It does this only under four stated Inputs (see conditional_on). Its k = 1 case is the Artin infinitude count restricted to positive prime bases.
artins-conjecture-on-primitive-roots.delivers: For (a), the claim proves the infinitude assertion for every admissible base, and the statement matches the list's. The list asks, for each integer a that is not a square and not -1, whether a is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes. The lower bound in (a) is positive in every sufficiently large dyadic interval, which gives infinitude. Restrictions: c_a and x_a depend on a, which the text states, and no uniformity in a is claimed. Negative bases other than -1 (for example -2, -3, -4) are covered by the signed squarefree decomposition a = d0 t^2 in the progression lemma, with the row d0 = -1 handling negative squares, and the Kummer bound is stated for |a| > 1. For (b), the claim gives infinitude only for positive prime bases, one or several at a time, and only conditionally on the four Inputs. It adds no unconditional case beyond (a) and does not cover composite or negative bases.
artins-conjecture-on-primitive-roots.remains: If (a) is correct, the infinitude statement of the bullet is fully covered and nothing in it remains open. Not established by either manuscript: the predicted order x/log x (the manuscripts prove x/(log x)^2 only), the asymptotic density with Artin's constant mentioned in the Wikipedia lead (outside the bullet), and any uniformity of c_a and x_a in a. For (b), the unconditional simultaneous case remains open, and so do all bases that are not positive primes.
artins-conjecture-on-primitive-roots.doubts: (a) The analytic core, Theorem 1.2, has no conductor or height cutoff and one width, 10^-6, for all cyclotomic fields containing mu_12 and all finite-order Hecke characters; the text says 'the width is common to all fields and characters in the statement'. The introduction describes the standard simultaneous zero-free regions as having logarithmic width and permitting at most one simple real exceptional zero (citing Thorner-Zaman, Theorem 3.1), and presents the common width as the new step. The text does not compare it with a published result of this strength. Cyclotomic Dedekind zeta functions factor into Dirichlet L-functions, so the statement as written also covers every Dirichlet L-function. The text does not discuss that consequence. The Hecke argument is described as built 'over each fixed F' from mechanisms of the companion 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis', which the introduction says treats Q(sqrt(-3)). The marked Type II estimate is imported from the Poisson-Dirichlet companion; the coefficient criterion's dependence is 'extracted' from that argument, and the introduction says the authors verify the character and frequency estimates themselves. (b) The four Inputs are hypotheses, and the text says their proofs lie in (a) and its companions, so (b) inherits the doubts in (a). The abstract's first sentence states the result without the condition, which appears only in its last sentence. The introduction counts four Inputs, but Input 2 has two parts, so there are five displayed hypotheses. Coverage: I did not read sections 02-06, the proof of Theorem 1.2, the fixed-progression construction in 12-construction.tex, or the appendix in full. A keyword search of those sections found no 'sketch' or 'left to the reader' style flags. The points above rest on the introduction, the reduction, the rough-Type II and sieve statements I read, and the Inputs of (b).; conditional on: (a) assumes no hypothesis of its own, but depends on work outside its text: (i) 'The Poisson-Dirichlet law for the prime factors of p-1', Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 5.2, for the one-sided marked Type II estimate; the text says its coefficient criterion (Lemma 10.2) extracts the coefficient dependence from that companion's argument. (ii) 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis', Part I, Sections 5-7, whose coefficient reflection and additive probe the text adapts over each cyclotomic field. (iii) Dunn and Radziwill, Section 5.1 and Appendix A, for theta comparison formulas. (iv) Kazhdan and Patterson's cubic theta representation with their erratum, and Patterson's cubic theta series, for the normalization. (v) The block-sieve and rough-density forms, adapted from 'BlockPaper' (Lemmas 2.9 and 7.4), with proofs included in the text. (b) assumes four Inputs, which it attributes to (a): the uniform Hecke zero-free assertion (the same as (a)'s Theorem 1.2: no zeros of L_F(s, eta) for Re s > 1 - 10^-6, for every finite-order Hecke character of a cyclotomic field containing mu_12); the marked Type II estimate in two parts, (i) the coefficient criterion (= (a)'s Lemma 10.2) and (ii) rough-factor cancellation (= (a)'s Proposition 10.3); the block sieve (= (a)'s Lemma 11.1); and the rough-number density (= (a)'s Lemma 11.2). Its splitting proof also takes the abelian tower argument and the prime-ideal count from (a)'s Section 9, equations (9.2) and (9.5)-(9.9), as cited.
artins-conjecture-on-primitive-roots.direction: proves the infinitude assertion for every admissible base (a); conditional proof of infinitude for positive prime bases, simultaneously (b)

standard-conjectures.what_happened: Only 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (6 Oct) addresses this. Its Corollary cc:standard claims two things for an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field K. First, for every prime l different from char(K), numerical and l-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on A. Second, for every rational ample divisor class h and every 0 <= r <= g/2, the rational symmetric form (x,y) -> (-1)^r deg(x y h^{g-2r}) on the primitive kernel P_h^r(A)_Q is positive definite after extension to R. The text calls the second part the Hodge standard conjecture for l-adic cohomology of abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic. The proof re-applies Milne's Theorem 3.3 of Milne 2002 ('Polarizations and Grothendieck's standard conjectures'), read with Theorem 2.1, Milne's addendum and the 1999 addenda, with the Hodge-type hypothesis supplied by the paper's CM theorem.
standard-conjectures.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-September-30-2026, Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-September-30-2026, Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-September-30-2026
standard-conjectures.delivers: The Hodge standard conjecture (positivity of the form on primitive algebraic classes, modulo numerical equivalence) for abelian varieties over algebraically closed fields in all characteristics, and Conjecture D (numerical = homological equivalence) for abelian varieties, stated with the l-adic homological equivalence for every l different from the characteristic. The problem's list records Wikipedia's status note for D as the Clozel case for infinitely many primes l; this manuscript states the claim for every prime l different from the characteristic, so the judge should check that comparison. Not addressed: Conjectures A and B (Lefschetz type) and Conjecture C (Kunneth type) for any variety, and Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties. The manuscript does not claim to settle the full bullet.
standard-conjectures.remains: Conjectures A, B and C for all smooth projective varieties, and for abelian varieties (not addressed). Conjecture D and the Hodge standard conjecture for smooth projective varieties other than abelian varieties.
standard-conjectures.doubts: The corollary's correctness depends on Milne's proof and the two cited addenda, which I did not read. The text does not discuss Conjectures A, B or C at all. The abstract says 'the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic', while the corollary states the positivity for l-adic cohomology; I read this as the same claim, stated with l-adic cohomology. No step is flagged as sketched.; conditional on: Milne's Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 2.1 of Milne 2002 (Annals of Mathematics), read with Milne's author addendum to the 2002 paper and the 1999 addenda (both externally hosted at jmilne.org; not in the repository). abundance-conjecture.what_happened: Fourteen manuscripts. The ones that bear on the bullet: (1) 'Log abundance in characteristic zero' (Sept 24) claims log abundance for normal projective lc pairs (X,B) over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero: B effective rational, K+B Q-Cartier and nef, then some positive Cartier multiple of K+B is globally generated. The B=0 klt case is the bullet. The proof is a dimension induction over C, with descent to other algebraically closed fields. It also claims canonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties over C in every dimension, and good log minimal models for pseudo-effective projective lc adjoints. (2) 'Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity' (Oct 6) claims, over C and conditionally on a stated subadditivity assumption, that an analytically nef K+Δ on a normal irreducible compact Kähler lc pair with effective rational Δ and Q-Cartier K+Δ is semiample, in every dimension. Projective varieties are compact Kähler, so Δ=0 gives the bullet over C, conditionally. (3) 'Conditional good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds' (Oct 6) has, in its projective appendix, conditional projective log abundance: normal projective lc over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field with nef Q-Cartier K+B is semiample, given logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity. Its main theorem is conditional good minimal models for klt compact Kähler fourfolds. (4) 'Abundance after nonvanishing for compact Kähler fourfolds' (Sept 27) claims that for a normal connected compact Kähler klt fourfold with effective rational Δ and analytically nef Q-Cartier K+Δ, K+Δ is semiample once κ(X,K+Δ)≥0 (nonvanishing is a hypothesis). If κ=0 the adjoint is trivial. Projectivity and Q-factoriality are not assumed. (5) 'Lifting sections from the reduced support of an adjoint' (Sept 27) claims: a supported-boundary lifting theorem for projective Q-factorial dlt pairs (positive Iitaka dimension when a Cartier multiple supported on the reduced boundary restricts to a semiample bundle on that whole boundary); abundance after nonvanishing for projective lc pairs of dimension at most 4 over C; a fourfold log abundance corollary for lc pairs of dimension at most 4 over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, which takes its nonvanishing from (6); and a conditional reduction in all dimensions, assuming smooth canonical nonvanishing in every dimension. (6) 'Fourfold nonvanishing by minimal metrics and moving jets' (Sept 27) claims canonical nonvanishing for smooth connected projective complex fourfolds (K pseudo-effective implies H^0(mK) nonzero for some m). Its Corollary 1.2 gives nonvanishing for projective lc pairs of dimension at most 4 with effective rational Δ and nef Q-Cartier K+Δ. (7) 'Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints' (Sept 27) claims zero-Lelong minimal semipositive metrics on pullbacks of nef Q-Cartier adjoints of projective klt pairs, and an H^1 injectivity theorem on smooth projective varieties. It is an analytic input, not an abundance statement. (8) 'Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi-Yau pairs' (Oct 5) claims, for each dimension d≥4 and finite coefficient set Φ, a uniform integer a(d,Φ) such that a(K+B) is Cartier and trivial for every connected projective slc log Calabi-Yau pair (K+B ~Q 0) with coefficients in Φ. With B=0 and X klt this covers klt varieties with K_X ~Q 0. (9) 'Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations' (Oct 3) claims a uniform pluricanonical degree m(d) whose complete system defines the Iitaka fibration of every smooth projective d-fold with κ≥0 (Theorem 1.1), and a uniform index a(d,Φ) for projective lc pairs with K+B ~Q 0 (Theorem 1.2). Both use the log-abundance paper. (10) 'Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators' (Oct 4) claims, for d≥5 and finite coefficients, a uniform degree at which the complete rounded system of an lc pair with κ≥0 generates the full Iitaka field. (11) 'Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations for fourfolds' (Sept 26) claims the four-dimensional finite-coefficient effective log Iitaka statement, and a uniform canonical index N_4 with N_4 K_X ~ 0 for normal projective klt fourfolds with K_X ~Q 0. (12) 'Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations' (Sept 27) gives denominator and effective-system bounds for log Calabi-Yau fibrations from lc pairs of dimension at most 4. (13) 'Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi-Yau pairs' (Sept 25) bounds the constant-field degree [k_S:k] of each component S of B with coefficient at least t. (14) 'Schnell fiber spaces and good canonical models' (Sept 24) proves the Campana-Peternell inequality κ(X)≥κ(D), and κ(X)=κ(F)+dim Y for fibre spaces under a pseudo-effectivity hypothesis. Items 12-14 make no semiampleness claim. For 12-14 I read only the abstracts and opening sections.

abundance-conjecture.delivers: For the bullet as worded (normal projective klt variety, nef canonical bundle, conclusion: semiample), the strongest claim is (1). It claims the bullet's case in every dimension over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with K_X Q-Cartier. The paper states this as a positive answer to the characteristic-zero log abundance conjecture. Its statement matches the list's in dimension and in class: klt is lc with Δ=0, nef is the same hypothesis, and semiample is the same conclusion. The bullet names no field, and the live article says over a field k. The claim reaches only algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields. Dimension at most 4 over such fields is also claimed by the fourfold corollary in (5), which takes nonvanishing from (6) and does not rely on the all-dimensional induction. The compact Kähler paper (2), the conditional appendix of (3), and the reduction in (5) give the bullet only under their stated premises. The rationally trivial special case, K_X ~Q 0, is also covered by the index statements (8), (9) and (11). Those give integral triviality of a multiple rather than semiampleness of a general nef class. A nef, numerically trivial K_X that is not Q-linearly trivial falls under (1) only.
abundance-conjecture.remains: If (1) is correct, the bullet is covered for algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero in every dimension. Still open for the bullet: positive characteristic, and characteristic-zero fields that are not algebraically closed. The bullet names none of these, and the family does not claim them. The all-dimensional coverage rests on (1) alone. If (1)'s induction failed, what would remain claimed is dimension at most 4, through (5) and (6), and the compact Kähler and conditional statements under their premises.
abundance-conjecture.doubts: (a) Abstract versus dependencies: the Uniform Pluricanonical abstract says 'We prove the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture in characteristic zero' and does not mention that the proof uses (1); the introduction says it does. The Uniform indices abstract says the paper 'resolves' the slc index conjecture and does not mention its reliance on the good-model theorem of (1). (b) The projective good-model section of the compact Kähler paper (03b) is a compressed argument that cites numbered theorems and lemmas of Fujino's analytic MMP paper (Theorem E, Theorem 8.3, Lemmas 11.13-11.17). I did not check those citations. (c) In the abundance-after-nonvanishing paper, the positive-Iitaka branch is delegated to Höring-Lazić-Lehn, and the finiteness argument for non-projective surface strata (returning chains, a groupoid that 'may have infinitely many arrows') is one paragraph. The paper calls the surface mechanism prior art. (d) The log-abundance paper's introduction says of the compatibility step: 'The proof must still identify the obstruction to lifting and show that these ordinary-variety results apply to the covering construction.' I did not check the sections where that argument is carried out. (e) The lifting paper's core argument (its supported-boundary theorem) is summarized in a few paragraphs of its introduction. I did not check its sections. (f) The lifting paper's introduction also states, without using it in the theorems, a conormal-period result for smooth fourfolds with nef K and κ=0 (no ν=2). The main theorem also assumes a pseudo-effective fourfold MMP (outside OpenAI preprint 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds') and effective fourfold abundance, which is (4). (4) Assumes κ≥0 (nonvanishing) as a hypothesis. Positive Iitaka dimension is delegated to Höring-Lazić-Lehn, Theorem 4.1 (external). The threefold floor input is Das-Ou, Corollary 1.3 (external). (5) The fourfold corollary uses (6), Corollary 1.2. The all-dimensional reduction assumes smooth canonical nonvanishing in every dimension (Hashizume's Conjecture 1.3). (6) Uses the moving-center lemmas 7.1-7.5 and Theorem 9.1 of (1), the analytic inputs of (7), and Hashizume's Theorem 1.4 for the lc extension. (8), (9), (10), (11) use the good-model theorem of (1) (Theorem 11.1 as cited); (8) also uses the normal index theorem of (9), external results of Birkar (2025), and Jiang-Liu for dimension at most 3. abundance-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts, both claiming the numerical-dimension-one case of threefold abundance in characteristic p>3 over an algebraically closed field. (1) 'Log abundance in numerical dimension one for threefolds in positive characteristic' (dated October 5, 2026) claims: for a projective log canonical threefold pair (X,B), with X normal, B an effective Q-divisor, K_X+B Q-Cartier, nef and of numerical dimension one, K_X+B is semiample (Theorem thm:main). Neither terminality nor Q-factoriality of X is assumed. The proof is by contradiction. After reductions (a dlt model, a terminal Q-factorial model, Xu's nonvanishing giving a nonzero effective N_0 with N_0 ~ m(K+B)), it assumes the nef dimension of N_0 is three. It then separates the boundary from N_0 (BNH=0, via bend-and-break), isolates a coefficient-one component by a partial MMP, proves torsion on the nonreduced Cartier cycle (adjunction plus surface abundance), and builds a smooth threefold V with a connected primitive nef cycle D that has torsion normal bundle and a canonical relation. It then invokes a cycle obstruction theorem stated as a black box from the companion (2). Nef dimension at most two is handled by Xu's cited theorems. (2) 'Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic' (dated September 24, 2026; called the companion in (1)) claims: for a normal projective Q-factorial terminal threefold X over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>3 with K_X nef and numerical dimension one, some positive Cartier multiple of K_X has at least two independent sections, so kappa(X,K_X)=1 and K_X is semiample (Theorem thm:main). Its proof is also by contradiction in the case of nef dimension three. It builds a smooth V and a connected snc primitive nef cycle D with torsion O_D(D) and a canonical relation near D. It shows T_V strongly semistable, c_2(V)·D=0 and uniform polar-part bounds, proves a Laurent-cohomology vanishing criterion, and concludes that the Picard group of the punctured formal neighbourhood of |D| is p-divisible while a degree homomorphism to Z is nonzero on it. The final semiampleness step and nef dimension at most two are taken from Xu's cited theorems.
abundance-conjecture.delivers: For the bullet (klt varieties, K_X nef, semiample, no boundary, every dimension, no field restriction) the manuscripts claim exactly one slice: threefolds X of numerical dimension one, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>3. Manuscript (1) with B=0 covers every klt, indeed lc, threefold with K_X nef and nu(K_X)=1 in that setting, with no terminality or Q-factoriality hypothesis. Manuscript (2) covers the terminal Q-factorial subcase and additionally states kappa(X,K_X)=1. Neither manuscript says it settles the abundance conjecture. Both say they prove the numerical-dimension-one case of threefold (log) abundance in this characteristic range. Their problem statements differ from the bullet's: (1) states log abundance for lc pairs with effective rational boundary (the bullet is its B=0 case, restricted to threefolds); (2) states abundance only for terminal Q-factorial threefolds, which is a subclass of the bullet's klt varieties. Both are stated over algebraically closed fields, and both are restricted to p>3.
abundance-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct, still open for the bullet: every dimension other than 3 (neither manuscript treats other dimensions); threefolds with nu(K_X)=0 (nef K_X numerically trivial, which needs torsion); threefolds with nu(K_X)=2 (only via Xu's 2026 theorem, cited, not proved in this family); threefolds with nu(K_X)=3 (nef and big, not treated); characteristic 0, 2 and 3 (p=2 and p=3 are excluded and characteristic 0 is not addressed); and fields that are not algebraically closed, except for the one-paragraph descent argument each manuscript gives.
abundance-conjecture.doubts: (1): The contradiction rests on the companion's obstruction. (1) says it applies to 'any cycle with the displayed properties' on the grounds that the companion's Section 2 retains only V, D, H_V, the torsion order and the canonical relation (foundations.tex:50-56, 66-70). The cycle constructed in (1) comes from a different, log canonical construction, so applicability depends on that reading of the companion. Several steps are compressed: the claim that the relative MMP output is not of fibre type and still has nef dimension three is given in a few sentences (foundations.tex:145-178); the 'for completeness' argument that very general points avoid the bad set (boundary.tex:55-66) is brief; the claim that removing an effective boundary from a dlt pair strictly increases discrepancy, used to get Y klt, is asserted in one sentence (isolation.tex:213-218); the isolation step is described as adapting the companion's Section 2.3 and Xu's partial-MMP formulation. The theorem is stated for algebraically closed k, and the descent from an uncountable closure is argued in one paragraph (foundations.tex:131-143). The bend-and-break bound 0 <= N·Gamma <= 4·NC/(-KC) is taken from Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl as stated. (2): The paper says 'We give the details that are relevant here' for slope calculus when D is only nef, not ample (slopes.tex:28-31). It says 'One can check' for the dual of a jet map and its index (jets.tex:182) and for a base-change square (laurent.tex:408). The omitted-lift combinatorics in the jet section are described by an illustrative picture (jets.tex:676-691). The semistability proof cites Xu-Zhang Lemma 2.10 'with the quantitative bend-and-break statement specified below' (slopes.tex:325), which is then stated (slopes.tex:372-380). The final semiampleness step (from kappa=1) uses Xu 2024 Theorem 1.6, not proved here. Q-factoriality is a stated hypothesis of the theorem but is not preserved by the field extension used in the proof; the text says modifications supply it when needed (preparation.tex:119-120).; conditional on: (1) depends on the cycle obstruction theorem (Theorem thm:obstruction, 'Cycle obstruction from the companion'), which (1) states without proof as a theorem and attributes to the companion's Proposition 2.1 and Sections 3-6 (cited as Corollary 5.4 and Proposition 6.8). The matching statements in (2) appear to be its form-vanishing corollary (Section 5) and its degree contradiction (Section 6); I did not verify the numbering against a compiled version. (1) also relies on Xu's nonvanishing and abundance theorems (Xu 2024, Theorems 1.4, 1.5, 1.8), Hashizume-Nakamura-Tanaka and Hacon-Witaszek MMP results (Hacon-Witaszek Theorem 1.2), Xu 2026's partial MMP and dlt lemmas, Posva's and Tanaka's surface abundance (Posva Theorem 3.1, Tanaka Theorem 0.1), and Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl bend-and-break (Theorem 1.1). (2) depends on Xu 2024 Theorems 1.4, 1.6 and 1.8, Xu 2026's nef reduction and partial MMP lemmas, the threefold MMP (Hacon-Xu, Hashizume-Nakamura-Tanaka, Hacon-Witaszek), Posva's and Tanaka's surface abundance, Xu-Zhang Lemma 2.10, Jovinelly-Lehmann-Riedl bend-and-break, Langer's Bogomolov inequality, and Katz's Cartier descent. (2) does not depend on (1).
abundance-conjecture.direction: proves a case (numerical dimension one, threefolds, characteristic p>3)

abundance-conjecture.what_happened: Four manuscripts; none states the bullet verbatim. (1) “Numerical Semiampleness of Nef Adjoint Divisors” (Oct 3 2026, build/main.tex, introduction Theorem thm:main): for a projective klt Q-pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with K_X+B pseudo-effective, M a nef Q-Cartier divisor on X and K_X+B+M nef, the divisor K_X+B+M is numerically equivalent to a semiample Q-Cartier divisor. With B=0 and M=0 this is the bullet’s case (K_X nef). The introduction then cites Fukuda’s theorem to say a semiample numerical representative makes K_X+B itself semiample, so for M=0 the manuscript claims K_X is semiample, conditionally on its log abundance input (see conditional_on). (2) “Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds” (Oct 6 2026, build/main.tex): for smooth connected compact Kähler X, a rational snc boundary B with coefficients below one, and a rational nef M, if K_X+B is pseudo-effective and K_X+B+M is nef, then c_1(K_X+B+M) equals, in real Bott–Chern cohomology, the first Chern class of a semiample rational line bundle. With B=0, M=0 this covers smooth projective varieties with nef K_X, but only numerically: the paper says it “does not assert semiampleness of the original adjoint”. Singular klt varieties are outside its scope. (3) “Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs” (Sept 24 2026, build/main.tex): for projective generalized lc Q-pairs over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a birational map to a model Y that extracts no divisors and does not lower discrepancies, with K_Y+B_Y+M_Y nef when the adjoint is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise. The Corollary with M=0 gives the ordinary lc case. Semiampleness is not in its theorem; the paper says the companion log abundance theorem [OpenAILogAbundance2026, Thm 1.1] makes K_Y+B_Y semiample on that model Y, not on X. (4) “Minimal models in numerical dimension one” (Sept 24 2026, build/paper.tex): for a smooth connected complex projective X of dimension n at least 3 with K_X pseudo-effective and Nakayama’s section-growth invariant κ_σ(X,K_X)=1 (fixed ample twist), a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips X ⇢ Y to a Q-factorial terminal Y with K_Y nef, with p*K_X = q*K_Y + E, E effective. A Corollary makes Y a good minimal model via the same companion log abundance theorem. It says nothing about semiampleness of K_X on X itself.

abundance-conjecture.delivers: Unconditionally, none of the four manuscripts establishes semiampleness of K_X on a projective klt variety X. The Oct 3 manuscript, if its inputs are granted, claims the bullet’s B=0, M=0 case in every dimension, including the smooth case, over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero; its stated theorem is numerical, and semiampleness of K_X is obtained only by citing Fukuda’s theorem. Its abstract calls the result the Generalised Abundance Conjecture of Lazić–Peternell, which is the M nonzero generalization of the bullet. The bullet names no field; the live article says a field k, and the manuscripts do not cover arbitrary fields of characteristic zero or characteristic p. The Kähler manuscript delivers only the numerical Bott–Chern statement for smooth compact Kähler manifolds, and for the projective case it says “Projective manifolds are covered by [P]”. The lc minimal-model and numerical-dimension-one manuscripts deliver nef minimal models on birational models; their semiampleness claims are for Y, and only through the companion log abundance theorem.
abundance-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct: (a) fields other than algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero are not covered by any of the four; (b) for the lc minimal-model and numerical-dimension-one manuscripts, semiampleness of K_X on X itself is not addressed; (c) for the Kähler manuscript, singular klt varieties are not covered, and semiampleness rather than numerical semiampleness of K_X is not established; (d) for the numerical-dimension-one manuscript, every case with κ_σ different from 1, and dimensions below 3, remain; (e) for the Oct 3 manuscript, nothing remains on the bullet’s klt, B=0, M=0 case beyond the numerical-to-semiample step, which depends on Fukuda’s theorem as cited.
abundance-conjecture.doubts: Oct 3: the text says its M=0 conclusion “is equivalent to ordinary klt abundance, which is an input to this proof”, and takes lc log abundance from [LA] as Theorem input:abundance. The abstract’s “We prove the Generalised Abundance Conjecture” therefore rests on that input. The main theorem is numerical (D ≡ L), and semiampleness of K_X for M=0 comes from citing Fukuda. The Frobenius comparison is said to “reproduce the comparison proof” of [LA] “with its uniformity conditions”. Kähler: the text says the statement does not assert semiampleness; the algebraic-dimension-zero case depends on Proposition zero:line-nonvanishing, which is stated under two line-subsheaf bounds that Lemma zero:cotangent-slope supplies, and the proof follows [K, Section 6] while giving its estimates. I did not check Sections 03, 04, 06 or most of 05. Minimal-models (lc): the text says the bounded-fibre theorem “only its reference form has bounded index”; the BFMT precedent is stated for klt singularities and the manuscript notes “the reference form here may be lc”; the transfer is credited to others. I read only Section 1 of twelve sections. Numerical-dimension-one: the finiteness of the canonical prefix comes from Lemma mmp:stabilization, a cycle-class dimension count adapted from [AHK07], a four-fold result; the introduction says the cycle arguments “do not assert termination of the concatenated programs”, so this step carries the finiteness claim in the theorem. Its semiampleness claim is conditional, as stated above.; conditional on: Oct 3 manuscript: (i) its Theorem input:abundance is log abundance for projective lc Q-pairs over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, cited as [LA] = OpenAI “Log abundance in characteristic zero”, Theorem 1.1; I did not read that paper. This statement contains the bullet’s klt, B=0 case, so the manuscript assumes it rather than proving it. (ii) The moving-jet and Frobenius results of [LA] (its Sections 7–9, Lemmas 7.1–7.5, Proposition 6.11, Theorem 9.1), which the manuscript adapts for the full-nef-dimension step (Theorem thm:terminal-big). (iii) The terminating minimal model programme for generalized klt pairs from [MM], which is the Minimal-models manuscript in this family (Theorem 1.1 and Section 3.3). (iv) Fukuda’s theorem [Fukuda, Theorem 0.1], to pass from numerical to actual semiampleness when M=0. (v) Published inputs such as BCHM and Birkar–Zhang. abundance-conjecture.what_happened: The family has one manuscript, 'Canonical ampleness of compact hyperbolic Kähler manifolds' (build/main.tex, dated 23 September 2026, author listed as OpenAI). Its Theorem 1.1 says: if X is a compact connected Kähler manifold of complex dimension n ≥ 1 and every holomorphic map ℂ → X is constant, then Kₓ is ample, so a positive power of Kₓ embeds X in projective space. The abstract calls this a positive resolution of Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in the smooth compact Kähler setting. The argument runs as follows. A maximizing-disc argument gives a uniform bound on the Poisson Ricci integral for all finite-area discs, which gives nefness of Kₓ through bounded plurisubharmonic canonical weights and a smoothing lemma (sections 'Extremal discs', 'Bounded canonical potentials and nefness', and the appendix on smoothing). A second use of the same disc identities gives a uniform lower bound on hⁿ/kⁿ for any Kähler metric h with Ricci curvature at least −h. With Aubin–Yau metrics in the classes 2πc₁(Kₓ) + t[k], this gives ∫c₁(Kₓ)ⁿ > 0. Nefness plus positive top self-intersection then give bigness and Moishezon-ness, Moishezon plus Kähler gives projectivity, and the absence of rational curves, via a Kodaira-lemma decomposition and the log cone theorem, upgrades bigness to ampleness. The same manuscript also states two corollaries that the main proof does not use. Corollary 1: for a compact connected Brody-hyperbolic Kähler manifold of dimension n ≥ 1, Kₓ^{⊗m} is globally generated for every m ≥ n+2. Corollary 2: under an extra semialgebraic hypothesis on the universal cover, X has a finite étale cover of the form (D/Γ₀) × F. The manuscript never mentions the abundance conjecture.
abundance-conjecture.delivers: For smooth compact connected Kähler manifolds of positive dimension with no nonconstant entire curves (these are projective by the same theorem; no singularities and no boundary divisor), the canonical bundle Kₓ is ample. Ampleness gives some positive multiple of Kₓ that is base-point free, so the conclusion of the bullet, semiampleness, holds in this class, with the hypothesis that Kₓ is nef derived from hyperbolicity rather than assumed. Corollary 1 additionally gives explicit base-point-freeness of Kₓ^{⊗m} for m ≥ n+2 in the same class, conditional as noted below. The statement is over ℂ. The bullet's general form (klt projective varieties with nef canonical bundle, possibly with boundary) is not what the manuscript states. The manuscript does not claim to settle the abundance conjecture; the overlap is the ampleness conclusion for one special class.
abundance-conjecture.remains: Still open, if the claim is correct, is the general bullet: (i) projective varieties with singular klt singularities; (ii) klt pairs with a boundary Δ and nef K + Δ; (iii) nef canonical bundles that are not ample (numerically trivial, nef and big but not ample, or Iitaka dimension strictly between 0 and n), since hyperbolicity excludes these cases; (iv) varieties over fields other than ℂ, including positive characteristic. Within the smooth Brody-hyperbolic class, no semiampleness question is left open if the claim is correct.
abundance-conjecture.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched and contains no explicit hedge. Points to weigh: (a) four cited statements are pinned to an unnamed 'authors' preprint' or 'author's preprint' of the cited work, not to a published version: Sukhov–Tumanov Section 4.1 (Cauchy estimates), Glöckner Theorem 2.3(ii),(d) (holomorphic implicit function theorem), Wu–Yau Proposition 8(i) and Lemma 6 (cohomological volume strategy), and Namikawa Theorem 6 (Moishezon projectivity with 1-rational singularities). The text does not say which version is meant. (b) The Poletsky–Rosay envelope is applied to ℓ = log|s|²ₖ on the complement of the zero section of the determinant bundle, which is globally unbounded. The text says the envelope theorem applies without boundedness, justified in one sentence by the cited Drinovec Drnovšek–Forstnerič formulation. (c) The area part of the Hessian identity rests on a weak boundary limit along radii chosen by an integrability argument, with an o((1−r)^{1/2}) estimate given in compressed form. The introduction calls boundary behaviour the main analytic difficulty. (d) The convexity claim in the radius-comparison lemma of the smoothing appendix is argued in a few sentences. (e) The introduction says nefness of Kₓ already follows from Ou2025 and Cao–Höring2020 under the absence of rational curves. The manuscript keeps its own disc proof of nefness, and says the further issue for ampleness is positive canonical volume.; conditional on: No hypothesis beyond the stated one (absence of nonconstant entire curves). The proof uses cited results without proving them: the Aubin–Yau negative-sign Monge–Ampère theorem; Demailly's holomorphic Morse inequalities; Poletsky–Rosay disc envelopes in the Drinovec Drnovšek–Forstnerič form; Kollár's log resolution theorem; Fujino's log cone theorem and Kleiman's criterion; Moishezon's projectivity theorem; and the standard Oka–Grauert, Wiener–Masani and Helson–Lowdenslager results. For the final ampleness step the text cites Diverio–Trapani Lemma 2.1 and Diverio Lemma 5.1, then gives its own argument. Corollary 1 is not used in the main theorem, but its proof depends on OpenAIFujita2026 Corollary 6.3 (Fujita freeness in all-powers form, exponent n+1). Corollary 2 depends on OpenAISemialgebraicCovers2026 Theorem 1.1. Neither of those two manuscripts was read here.
abundance-conjecture.direction: proves a special case: Kₓ is ample, hence semiample, for smooth compact Kähler Brody-hyperbolic manifolds; this is Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in that class

fujita-conjecture.what_happened: The family has one manuscript, 'Fujita's freeness conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its main theorem: for X a smooth connected projective variety over ℂ of dimension n ≥ 1 and L an ample line bundle on X, Kₓ + (n+1)L is generated by its global sections. A corollary (cor:all-powers) deduces that Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every integer m ≥ n+1, by applying the main theorem to X × ℙʳ with r = m−n−1 and the ample bundle L ⊠ O(1); the adjoint bundle there is (Kₓ + mL) ⊠ O(n), and its restriction to X × {z} is Kₓ + mL. The text gives ℙⁿ with L = O(1) as the sharpness example: Kₓ + (n+1)L is trivial while Kₓ + nL has no nonzero sections. The proof is by contradiction at a point x. (i) An 'ordinary-order alternative' shows that failure of generation at x forces a strict asymptotic inequality for the mean ordinary order of bases of H⁰(X, mL). (ii) The proof minimizes an exponential functional over bases of H⁰(X, mL) and weighted monomial valuations whose centers contain x, for a fixed t < n+1. It shows the minimum is attained and has bounded discrepancy. (iii) A tangential variation of a minimizer, a uniform lower estimate on restriction spaces, and a discrete Brunn–Minkowski inequality show that minimizers have center exactly {x} in arbitrarily large degrees. (iv) A rational supporting profile is used to build an effective SNC boundary and a reduced divisor S over x on which the boundary coefficient equals the log discrepancy and is strictly smaller on neighbouring components. (v) Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing, in Fujino's logarithmic form, lifts a nonzero value from S, and descent gives a section of Kₓ + (n+1)L that is nonzero at x. This contradicts the assumed failure.
fujita-conjecture.delivers: For the freeness (global generation) part of the list's problem: for every smooth complex projective variety X of dimension n and every ample L on X, Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every m ≥ n+1. The threshold n+1 is the sharp one, per the sharpness example. Restrictions: the setting is smooth projective varieties over ℂ, not compact complex manifolds with a positive holomorphic bundle; L must be ample; the theorem assumes connectedness, which the text says only fixes notation (applies componentwise). The manuscript states its result as a proof of Fujita's freeness conjecture. Its freeness statement matches part (a) of the list's problem, at threshold m ≥ n+1. The manuscript does not claim the whole problem as the list words it: the list's problem also covers very ampleness (part (b)), which the Introduction says is not asserted. The list's compact-complex-manifold formulation is not addressed in the manuscript. The research pass's reduction (a positive holomorphic bundle on a compact complex manifold makes it projective via Kodaira's embedding theorem, with L ample) would bring it into scope, but the manuscript does not state this reduction.
fujita-conjecture.remains: Part (b) of the problem: very ampleness of Kₓ + mL for m ≥ n+2, using the research pass's threshold. The Introduction explicitly says the manuscript does not assert separation of points or tangent directions, or the very-ampleness part of Fujita's conjecture. The compact-complex-manifold formulation is not treated directly in the text. Nothing is claimed for m ≤ n, and the sharpness example shows that m = n cannot work in general.
fujita-conjecture.doubts: (1) Several steps are given in condensed form. The constructibility half of the closed-threshold-locus lemma (lem:lct-family) is argued by saying it parallels the proof of Demailly–Kollár, with a stratification sketched in a few sentences. The multiplicity bound in lem:min-initials is justified in two sentences via a general curve. The claim that every fixed ball meets j⁻¹Hⱼ along the subsequence, which the ordinary-order alternative relies on, is argued in one paragraph without explicit constants. The compactness step in the existence of minimizers asserts that section orders are linear in the weights on the fixed model. (2) The final lift is described as following the discrepancy-and-vanishing strategy of Fujita 1993, §1(1.6), but the text writes out the lift itself and does not separately verify the adaptation. (3) The claim is much stronger than the bounds the Introduction itself cites. The sharpest general bounds it lists are of order n: Han, m ≥ ⌈C₀n⌉ with C₀ ≈ 1.776, and Ghidelli–Lacini, m ≥ n(log log n + 2.34) for n ≥ 2. The Introduction says the sharp bound is known for curves, for surfaces (Reider), and for dimensions three to five (Ein–Lazarsfeld, Kawamata, Ye–Zhu). The all-dimension claim is stated without hedging. (4) The Introduction records that a 2024 preprint by Chan, claiming a stronger intersection-number form, was withdrawn because a local extension argument did not guarantee the required vanishing order. The manuscript's final step is also a vanishing-based extension from a divisor over x. The text does not say explicitly how that failure is avoided beyond the isolation lemma. (5) The abstract does not state the connectedness hypothesis that the main theorem includes. The text says this only fixes notation, which I take at its word.
fujita-conjecture.direction: proves the freeness conjecture (global generation) at the sharp threshold m ≥ n+1; the very-ampleness part is not addressed
