nagatas-conjecture-on-curves.what_happened: Four manuscripts are in the family; the first is the direct match and the others bear on it only through Seshadri forms. (a) 'Nagata's conjecture for plane curves' (folder Nagatas-Conjecture-for-Plane-Curves-September-23-2026, dated 23 September 2026). Theorem 1.1 (thm:main) claims that for every integer r ≥ 10 there is a countable union E_r of proper Zariski-closed subsets of U_r, the space of ordered r-tuples of distinct points of ℙ²_ℂ, with nonempty complement, such that for every tuple outside E_r, every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d ≥ 1 and all nonnegative integers m_i with multiplicity at p_i at least m_i satisfies d√r > Σm_i. Reducible and nonreduced curves are included, and the multiplicities need not be equal. Corollary cor:sesha (consequences section) reads this on the blow-up: √r·H − ΣE_i is strictly nef with self-intersection zero, so the multipoint Seshadri constant of O(1) is exactly 1/√r. The same corollary proves the matching upper bound by counting: forms of degree ⌈√r(n+1)⌉ with multiplicity n at all r points exist. Corollary cor:fields extends the statement to every uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, again with nonempty complement. (b) 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (23 September 2026) does not treat plane curves as such. Read as a specialization to S = ℙ² with L = O(1) (so L² = 1), its main theorem gives ε = 1/√r at very general tuples for every sufficiently large r, with no threshold computed. That specialization is my reading; the manuscript does not state it. (c) 'Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic' (5 October 2026). Its dimension-two remark (rem:surfaces) asserts the same equality for ℙ² at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of characteristic p, for r at or above a threshold. (d) 'Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions' (5 October 2026) treats dimension n ≥ 3 only and does not bear on plane curves.
nagatas-conjecture-on-curves.delivers: If the claim holds, it delivers the strict inequality of problem_asks (1) in full: for r ≥ 10 (the list's r > 9), at very general tuples over ℂ, every plane curve with multiplicities m_i at those points satisfies d > (1/√r)Σm_i. The manuscript says it establishes 'Nagata's conjecture in its strict, nonhomogeneous form', and its theorem covers every r ≥ 10, including the non-square r the list treats as open and the square r ≥ 16 that Nagata proved earlier. The part the list calls open is the degree lower bound, and that is the part claimed. The matching existence of curves is covered only by the counting upper bound in cor:sesha, which gives curves whose ratio tends to 1/√r. Field scope: the main theorem is over ℂ, and cor:fields extends it to uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. The list allows only positive multiplicities; the manuscript allows zero, which is a weaker-looking but equivalent statement for this purpose. Read as the specialization in (b), the surfaces manuscript gives the Seshadri form only for sufficiently large r with no threshold, so it covers less than the Nagata paper does.
nagatas-conjecture-on-curves.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing in problem_asks (1) remains open over ℂ or over uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, at very general tuples. Not covered: (i) tuples that are not very general. The exceptional set E_r is a countable union of proper closed subsets, chosen simultaneously for all degrees and multiplicity vectors, and it is not given explicitly. (ii) Countable fields and positive characteristic, which the Nagata paper does not treat. The positive-characteristic paper gives the Seshadri form for large r only, at geometric generic tuples. (iii) Exact existence of curves attaining the bound for each degree. The manuscript proves only the asymptotic counting upper bound in cor:sesha.

machine_checked.scope:
Nagata's conjecture asserts that a nonzero effective plane curve of degree $d$, with multiplicities at least $m_i$ at $r\ge10$ very general points, satisfies $\sum_i m_i<d\sqrt r$.

The formalization establishes this inequality simultaneously for all curves and multiplicity vectors outside one countable union of proper Zariski-closed exceptional sets with nonempty complement. Reducible curves, repeated components, and unequal multiplicities are included, in both effective-curve and homogeneous-polynomial formulations. The formalization also includes the passage from homogeneous effective cycles to equations.

The maximality question asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant reaches the upper bound $\sqrt{L^2/r}$ at very general points once $r$ is sufficiently large. The formalized result establishes this for every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$ and ample line bundle $L$.

For every $r$ above a threshold depending on $(S,L)$, it gives a countable union of proper closed exceptional sets with nonempty complement. Outside it, the constant is $\sqrt{L^2/r}$ and the boundary class defining this Seshadri constant on the point blowup is nef. The threshold is not explicit or uniform over all surfaces.

nagatas-conjecture-on-curves.doubts: No step is flagged as sketched, conditional or omitted. A search of the proof sections for 'sketch', 'omit', 'routine', 'verify', 'assum' and similar terms found no such flags. Two points bear on trust. First, the key nonsquare step (contract a slice-width polygon, and absorb the integer endpoint error by passing to a common power of the curve) is stated in one paragraph of the introduction and worked out in Sections 02–04, which I did not read in full. Second, the proof uses theta-function product identities. The text says it proves these itself in the normalization it needs, citing Rosengren only for conventions.
nagatas-conjecture-on-curves.direction: proves the conjecture: the strict Nagata inequality for all r ≥ 10 at very general tuples over ℂ

nagata-biran-conjecture.what_happened: The direct match is 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (23 September 2026). Its Theorem (thm:main) claims that for every smooth integral complex projective surface S and every ample line bundle L on S, there is an integer r_0(S,L) such that for each r ≥ r_0 there is a countable union Z_r of proper Zariski-closed subsets of U_r (ordered r-tuples of distinct points of S), with nonempty complement, such that for every tuple outside Z_r the class π*L − √(L²/r)·ΣE_i is nef on the blow-up. Hence ε(S,L; p_1,…,p_r) = √(L²/r) at those tuples. The universal bound ε ≤ √(L²/r) holds at every tuple and every r (Lemma sesha-upper, in nef.tex), so the content is the lower bound. Corollary cor:fields (nef.tex) extends the statement to smooth integral projective surfaces over any uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. The abstract calls this a positive resolution of the qualitative Nagata–Biran conjecture for surfaces. The introduction says that Harbourne (2003) already gave maximality for all sufficiently large r with rL² a square, for very ample L. The paper's own theorem covers all sufficiently large r, including the other values. The positive-characteristic paper's dimension-two remark (rem:surfaces) says the same conclusion holds for n = 2 at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of characteristic p, for r at or above a threshold depending on (S,L). The higher-dimensional paper ('Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions', 5 October 2026) treats only dimension n ≥ 3, with value (L^n/r)^{1/n} at very general tuples, and does not address surfaces.
nagata-biran-conjecture.delivers: If the claim holds, it establishes the qualitative Nagata–Biran statement for smooth integral complex projective surfaces. For each ample L there is an r_0 such that, for every r ≥ r_0, the Seshadri constant equals the stated value at very general r-tuples. The manuscript writes the value as √(L²/r), where L² is the self-intersection number. The list writes d/√r with d 'the degree' of L. The two agree only if d = √(L²), for example O(1) on ℙ², where L² = 1. The manuscript uses no letter d. The equality is exact for each large r, not merely asymptotic, and the upper bound holds at all tuples. The manuscript states that it resolves the conjecture positively for surfaces, and the list's 'sufficiently large r' regime matches r ≥ r_0. On scope, the list says 'a smooth algebraic surface' without qualification. The theorem covers smooth integral complex projective surfaces, and the corollary covers smooth integral projective surfaces over uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero.
nagata-biran-conjecture.remains: If the claim is correct, the following remain. (i) Points: equality holds only off a countable union of proper closed subsets, that is, at very general tuples. The list's unqualified 'the points p_1,…,p_r' is not covered at arbitrary tuples, and the manuscript claims nothing for particular tuples. (ii) Surfaces: non-projective smooth algebraic surfaces, countable fields, and positive characteristic are not covered by this manuscript. The positive-characteristic paper's dimension-two remark covers characteristic p only at the geometric generic tuple, not at very general tuples. (iii) Threshold: r_0(S,L) is an existence statement that depends on the chosen nodal divisor and parameters. The manuscript gives no explicit bound and no uniformity over surfaces. (iv) The sharper threshold prediction of Strycharz-Szemberg–Szemberg, which the introduction cites as a stronger form of the conjecture, is not claimed.

nagata-biran-conjecture.doubts: The threshold r_0 is defined through the nodal divisor and lattice-direction choices made in the node, compression and lattice sections. Those sections carry the content, and I did not read them in full. A search of them found no sketch or omission flags. The introduction presents the construction for each sufficiently large r as tuned to a primitive lattice direction, with a torus subgroup of index r that need not be a square grid. The text does not say how large r_0 must be. The plane Nagata manuscript (OpenAINagata2026) is cited only in the introduction, as a separate refinement of the threshold and the strict inequality; I found no use of it in the proof sections. The introduction describes prior results (Harbourne 2003, and Roé's transfer, which assumes plane maximality) as context. It says the argument treats arbitrary polarizations directly rather than through them.

zariski-lipman-conjecture.what_happened: The family is a single manuscript, 'A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf'. Its Theorem 1 (thm:main) claims that there exist a finitely generated normal integral C-algebra A of Krull dimension two and a maximal ideal m of A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A (free of rank two) and A_m not regular. The argument has two steps. (1) Proposition 'analytic-counterexample' builds a normal complex surface germ (X,x), smooth off x, with free holomorphic tangent sheaf of rank two. It takes a smooth genus-21 curve C with normal bundle L⁻¹, deg L = 10, L⁴ ≅ K_C; prescribes finite jets of two vector fields on a neighbourhood of C by finitely many holomorphic flows; glues these to a Hausdorff surface neighbourhood Y of C; lifts the jets holomorphically using vanishing of H¹ on the ideal filtration; and contracts C to x by Grauert's criterion. The text gives C² = −10, canonical discrepancy −5 for C, and p_g ≥ 33 (Remark 'invariants'). (2) Proposition 'algebraization' produces an affine normal A with the same completed local ring as (X,x) at the marked point, a principal affine neighbourhood on which Der_C(A) ≅ A^d with d = 2, and smoothness away from that point. The proof uses a finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix, which the paper proves itself, together with Artin approximation over a henselization.
zariski-lipman-conjecture.delivers: Disproves the statement as listed, in its affine form. The claim is a normal affine complex surface Spec A whose coordinate ring has free derivation module Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A, and which is singular at m because A_m is not regular. The manuscript says the result 'disproves the Lipman–Zariski conjecture in characteristic zero'. Its formulation matches the list: Der_C(A) is Hom_A(Ω¹_{A/C}, A), the hypothesis is freeness of the whole module, and the conclusion (smoothness) fails at a closed point. The introduction states the conjecture with 'locally free tangent sheaf'. Global freeness is a stronger hypothesis than local freeness, so the same example refutes that form too. The text also gives the analytic germ (the complex-space version) and the local ring A_m, whose derivations are free (Der_C(T) ≅ T^d in the proof). The text states that Spec A can be chosen smooth away from m. Normality of A is consistent with Lipman's theorem, which the introduction cites as showing that free derivations force normality.
zariski-lipman-conjecture.remains: If the claim holds, the listed statement is refuted and no part of it stays open. Not addressed by the text: the generalisation with reflexive p-forms; graded variants (the text remarks only that Hochster's graded theorem excludes getting this example from a positively graded cone); and higher dimensions. The introduction cites van Straten and Steenbrink as proving the isolated-singularity case in dimension at least three, so any higher-dimensional counterexample must have non-isolated singularities, and the manuscript does not treat that. No explicit equations for A are given.
zariski-lipman-conjecture.doubts: (a) The algebraization proof states that Der_C(T)⊗T̂ ≅ Der^cont(T̂,T̂) ≅ T̂^d 'is an equality obtained from finite presentations; it does not identify ordinary algebraic differentials of a power-series ring with its continuous differentials'. Freeness descent passes through this identity, and the text itself flags the distinction. (b) The finite-determinacy lemma with a relation matrix is proved in the paper rather than cited. The text presents it as a variant of Hironaka's and Artin's methods, 'including fixed estimates that avoid a complete-intersection hypothesis'. Its proof is an iterative improvement argument whose constants are fixed abstractly (by Artin–Rees), with no explicit values. (c) Several verifications are compressed. Closedness of the gluing graphs ends with 'Possible fiber boundaries cause no difficulty'. The order-two obstruction is settled by 'the following calculation evaluates all four' tests. Higher-order steps are given as formulas without all intermediate expansions. (d) Several existence steps rest on genericity ('general', 'sufficiently small', Bertini) and give no explicit parameters. (e) The introduction cites Bergner and Graf's inequality p_g − g − b ≤ 2 without stating what it implies. The claim that the example lies 'beyond' that criterion depends on reading it as a smoothness criterion. I found no inconsistency between the abstract, the introduction, Theorem 1 and the proof sections I read.; conditional on: None for the main theorem beyond published results the proof cites (Grauert's contraction and formal-function theorems, Artin's approximation theorem, Cartan's Theorem B, Serre's GAGA comparison, Cutkosky's excellence result). No other manuscript in the family is needed for the main theorem. Two corollaries depend on external results: the log-Kodaira-dimension corollary (algebra:log-kodaira) depends on Biswas–Gurjar–Kolte 2014, Theorem 0.1(1); the derivation-blowup corollary (algebra:derivation-blowups) depends on Villamayor's description as recalled in Barajas–Chávez-Martínez–Romano-Velázquez (arXiv:2510.07607), §1.6, Theorem 1.17. Neither is needed for the main claim.
zariski-lipman-conjecture.direction: disproves the conjecture (affine, dimension two, characteristic zero)
zariski-lipman-conjecture.object: Yes, but not explicit. Spec A is never written down. It is produced by existence arguments: a general genus-21 curve C on P¹×P¹ (Bertini and 'general' parameter conditions), a gluing of finitely many holomorphic flows, Grauert's contraction, and Artin approximation over a henselization followed by an étale shrinking. The analytic germ (X,x) is likewise non-explicit. Several choices are made by 'sufficiently general' or 'sufficiently small' conditions without explicit values.

nakai-conjecture.what_happened: The manuscript ('A singular normal affine surface with free tangent sheaf') says nothing about rings of differential operators, D(V), or Nakai's conjecture. A search of its build sources finds no mention of either. Its only claim in this area is the Lipman–Zariski counterexample in the entry above: a normal affine surface A with Der_C(A) ≅ A⊕A and A_m not regular.
nakai-conjecture.delivers: No claim about the Nakai hypothesis or conclusion. The manuscript does not show that the ring of differential operators of A, or of any other variety, is generated by its order-one operators. The family bears on Nakai only through the implication that the problem's context cites, namely that Nakai's conjecture implies Zariski–Lipman (Becker; Rego). If that implication holds, refuting Zariski–Lipman as this family does would also refute Nakai's conjecture. The manuscript neither states nor uses that route, and it does not verify the Nakai hypothesis for A. So the family does not settle Nakai on its own argument.
nakai-conjecture.remains: All of the Nakai problem as far as these manuscripts go: whether any singular complex variety, including the constructed A, has its ring of differential operators generated by derivations, and the order-n form for n ≥ 2 quoted in the problem context.
nakai-conjecture.doubts: The manuscript does not discuss differential operators at all, so nothing in the text checks the Nakai hypothesis for any variety. Any reading that counts this family as refuting Nakai depends entirely on the external implication.; conditional on: Bearing on Nakai requires the implication Nakai ⇒ Zariski–Lipman, which the manuscript neither states nor proves. I did not check the cited source (arXiv:2604.24508) and did not search for it. It also requires that the ring of differential operators of the constructed A, or of a variety derived from it, is generated by derivations, which the text does not address.
nakai-conjecture.direction: no direct direction; refutes Zariski–Lipman, which bears on Nakai only via the cited implication

are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.what_happened: Five manuscripts, all about fourfolds, each claiming a termination result in dimension four. None treats dimension five or higher. (a) 'Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 7, 2026; main theorem thm:main): for a normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X_0 with effective rational boundary B_0 of coefficients in [0,1], and a rational b-divisor represented by an analytically nef Q-Cartier divisor on a projective model, with (X_0, B_0+M) generalized log canonical, every sequence of flips X_i -> Z_i <- X_{i+1} (projective small maps with connected fibres, Z_i normal compact Kähler, neither map an isomorphism, -D_i f_i-ample, D_{i+1} f_i^+-ample) is finite. M=0 gives the ordinary lc case. (b) 'Termination of generalized-canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; build/build/paper.tex, theorem thm:termination): the same conclusion with boundary coefficients in [0,1) and generalized canonical hypotheses (every log discrepancy on X_0 positive, exceptional ones at least 1). (c) 'Termination for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary' (September 24, 2026): for a projective lc fourfold with rational boundary over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, (i) every negative extremal ray has its contraction and, when birational, a positive model; (ii) every permitted program has finitely many birational steps for every choice of rays, where a permitted program steps by contracting a negative extremal ray of relative Picard number one, followed by a divisorial contraction, a projective small flip, or a mixed step; (iii) maximal programs end at a nef lc model or a Mori fibre space. No Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity is assumed. (d) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (October 6, 2026; theorem thm:finite): for a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with klt effective rational boundary, every maximal program of ordinary negative steps (projective divisorial contractions and flips of D-negative extremal rays) terminates. The endpoint is nef when K+Δ is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a projective Mori fibre space over a base of dimension below four. Its finiteness of flip tails is taken from (a), via its Corollary repair:cor:existing. (e) 'Finite ordinary minimal model programs on compact Kähler fourfolds' (September 24, 2026; an earlier paper with the same title as (d)): for the same klt Kähler setting, there exists one finite ordinary program, obtained by a suitable choice of steps, with the same endpoint classification. It does not claim termination for every choice.
are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.revisions: 3 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Termination-of-generalized-log-canonical-flips-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026, Termination-of-generalized-canonical-flips-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026, Finite-ordinary-minimal-model-programs-on-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-5-2026
are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.delivers: Dimension four only, in the stated classes. (a) and (b) answer no for the flip sequences they describe: on Kähler, globally Weil Q-factorial fourfolds with a fixed rational nef b-divisor, no infinite sequence of such flips exists. They need no pseudo-effectivity or scaling, and the flips need not be extremal and the Z_i need not share a base. (c) answers no for every permitted program, hence for flips occurring as steps of such programs, on projective lc fourfolds with rational boundary, without Q-factoriality. Its singularity class is wider than (d)'s, but its flips must each contract a relative Picard number one extremal ray. (d) answers no for every maximal ordinary program on klt Kähler fourfolds: an infinite run would contain an infinite tail of flips, which (d) excludes by citing (a). Its divisorial steps are finite by a cycle count. (e) gives only existence of one finite program and says nothing about infinite sequences in general. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the bullet as the list words it. (c) says it proves 'the projective four-dimensional case of the Termination of Flips Conjecture for ordinary log canonical pairs with rational boundary'. (e) says it gives 'an affirmative solution of the finite-program form of the rational klt fourfold minimal model conjecture' in the Kähler category, and does not state that form. Against the bullet's parts: (1) dimensions: only n = 4 is treated; (2) objects: flips of pairs in the classes above, not all flips; (3) existence is not asked, but (a) and (b) state they do not assert existence of contractions or flips, while (c) and (d) construct the steps they use; (4) each 'no' covers only its class.
are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.remains: If the claims hold, still open for this bullet: every dimension n >= 5. In dimension four: flip sequences outside the classes above, including non-Q-factorial ambients for (a), (b), (d) and (e); non-Kähler ambients or non-projective flips for (a) and (b); boundaries with coefficients outside [0,1], non-lc pairs for (c), and non-klt pairs for (d) and (e); varying nef data for (a) and (b); arbitrary flip sequences that are not programs in (c), (d) and (e); flips whose negative contraction has relative Picard number above one, in (c); existence of flips in (a) and (b); termination for every choice of steps in (e). No manuscript treats the footnote's class directly: klt flips, projective over one fixed normal base. None of them fixes a base, and (a), (b), (d) and (e) add Kähler and global Weil Q-factoriality hypotheses.
are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.doubts: (1) (a) and (d) depend on each other: (d) uses (a)'s flip theorem for infinite flip tails, and (a) uses (d)'s special-termination and relative-program results. (d)'s Section 6 opening states that those results do not depend on its finite-program theorem. The loop is between papers, and that assertion is the one a reader must check. (2) (d)'s intrinsic formulation, with a canonical rational line bundle in place of a canonical divisor, is argued in one paragraph that ends 'leaves that proof unchanged'. (3) (b) says it 'reproduces these arguments in full and invokes no termination theorem', yet its negativity, terminal-smoothness and cycle-comparison inputs are cited to (e). (4) The introduction of (a) summarises its branch and difficulty estimates by method (Quot parameters, local factorisation, purity). The statements of the sections that carry them are not verified here. (5) (c)'s field-transfer lemma gives its key degree-constancy step with alternative justifications ('or follows from constancy of its Euler characteristic') and is compressed. (6) (e) claims an 'affirmative solution' of a conjecture whose form the text does not state.; conditional on: (a) cites from (d), without proving them: special termination for generalized dlt pairs in dimension four (its Theorem 11.3), relative continuation and finite runs (Propositions 9.7 and 9.9), exact extraction (Proposition 9.11), crepant gdlt modification (Proposition 11.4), and low places (Lemma 4.2(i)). It cites from (b): the common-model construction (Proposition 2.1), analytic negativity (Lemma 2.2) and terminal smoothness in codimension two (Lemma 2.3). Its difficulty and branch steps follow the projective methods of ProjectiveLCFourfolds, the companion (c), at Section 3 Proposition 3.4, Definition 4.2, Lemma 4.3, Section 5 Lemma 5.2, Section 6.1 and Section 7, with analytic steps supplied. (b) relies on Wang's analytic negativity lemma (external), and on (e)'s Lemma 2.3(i), Lemma 4.4 and Section 4.1. (d) relies on (a)'s Theorem 1.1 to exclude infinite flip tails, through its Corollary repair:cor:existing, and on its own relative and special-termination sections. (c) relies only on published inputs listed in its introduction: cone and contraction theorems, BCHM, Birkar's lc flip and complemented-pair existence results, surface mld ACC, dlt special termination, and Hodge theory. Its endpoint consequences (semiampleness, complements, Cartier sections) use three OpenAI companion preprints that are not part of its termination claim. (e) relies on Hacon and Xie (arXiv:2607.24986, July 2026) for the contractions and for finiteness of marked models away from scaling parameter zero, on Birkar (2009) for the limiting-model strategy, and on Matsumura and Zhong.
are-infinite-sequences-of-flips-possible.direction: proves termination of flip sequences in dimension four for the stated classes, answering no there only; (e) proves only existence of one finite program

zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts, each claiming a negative answer to Zariski's question whether embedded topology determines multiplicity for complex hypersurface germs. (1) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three' (dated 24 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there is a finite N > 3 divisible by eight (the text gives N = 4s₀ + 16, where s₀ is the variable count of two seed polynomials fixed by an integer relation it does not evaluate) and two reduced polynomials f₁, f₂ with real coefficients, weighted homogeneous for positive rational weights, each with an isolated critical point at the origin, with ord₀f₁ = 2, ord₀f₂ = 3, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂᴺ, V(f₁), 0) ≅ (ℂᴺ, V(f₂), 0). The construction builds sums of chain singularities from an integer relation among rational weights, matches the spectra modulo 2, obtains an integral Seifert-form isometry (Steenbrink/Némethi and Hertling–Mase/Orlik–Randell for the separate real and integral identifications, then a single integral isometry by strong approximation), applies Levine's classification of simple spherical knots, and extends the link equivalence to an ambient homeomorphism by a weighted cone map. Corollaries in the same manuscript (outside this problem's scope): f₁ and f₂ are topologically right equivalent, Arnold's Hessian-corank question is answered negatively, and initial-form Milnor fibres differ after adding t². (2) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five' (dated 27 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there are reduced convergent holomorphic germs f₄, f₅ : (ℂ⁴, 0) → (ℂ, 0), each with an isolated critical point at 0, with ord₀f₄ = 4, ord₀f₅ = 5, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂ⁴, V(f₄), 0) ≅ (ℂ⁴, V(f₅), 0). The construction starts from the plane curve h = T(X − T²)(X − 2T²) and two degree-four finite graph maps π₀, π₁, whose pullbacks are plane curves of the same embedded type with isometric integral Seifert forms. It smooths the cone yz = w⁴ and adds w(y^a + z^b) to h, with a and b given by formulas in an integer n₀ fixed by congruences. The integral Seifert congruence is obtained by strong approximation, the link equivalence by Kato's Theorem B on Milnor open books of S⁷, and the ambient homeomorphism by an analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4).
zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.delivers: For the pair form (two varieties at singular points that are topologically equivalent have equal multiplicity), both manuscripts claim a counterexample for complex hypersurface germs with isolated critical points: multiplicities 2 and 3 in ℂᴺ for some N > 3 divisible by eight (so N ≥ 8), and multiplicities 4 and 5 in ℂ⁴. An ambient homeomorphism of pairs carries V(f) onto V(g), so these pairs are topologically equivalent in the list's sense; the counterexample therefore reaches the list's pair form for reduced hypersurface germs. Both manuscripts describe the result as a negative answer to Zariski's embedded question (paper 1 calls it the 'embedded Zariski multiplicity conjecture'). The statement they prove is the classical hypersurface form, not the list's unrestricted 'varieties'. The family form (b) is not addressed: neither manuscript constructs a topologically equisingular family, and paper 1 says its pair cannot be joined by a μ-constant family and that arbitrary equivalent pairs do not reduce to the family problem.
zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.remains: (b) the family form, i.e. whether a topologically equisingular family of singular points has constant multiplicity, is not addressed by either manuscript. (c) Dimension three (ℂ³) is stated by both to remain untreated. Paper 1 does not cover N = 5, 6, 7 or N ≡ 0 mod 8 other than its unspecified N. Paper 2 is specific to N = 4. Plane curves (n = 2) are classically positive per paper 2's introduction (Zariski 1932), so the examples do not reach them. Non-hypersurface varieties, non-isolated singularities, and real or algebraic (non-holomorphic) varieties are not treated. Paper 1 says its construction is not intended to minimize the dimension.
zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.doubts: Paper 1: (i) the dimension N is not computed, so the claim is existential; the text says N 'is not intended to minimize' the dimension. (ii) The seed relation rests on finite calculations (a 1118-column cutoff matrix, rank over F₁₀₀₉, an adjugate of an 868-column minor), and the text says a supplied Python program checks them. The repository README says these checks 'cover the finite arithmetic, not the lattice-theoretic or topological arguments'. I did not open or run the programs. (iii) The abstract's topological right equivalence is a corollary, not part of Theorem 1.1, and the source homeomorphism is 'not claimed to be holomorphic or bi-Lipschitz' and need not coincide with the ambient map. (iv) Several results are cited to literature versions, e.g. 'arXiv v3' for Budur et al. Paper 2: (i) the authors flag a limit on a step: 'we do not assert that h is submersive through every value in the disk at θ = 0'; sublevel totals are then isotoped as manifolds with corners. (ii) Thresholds are stated as 'sufficiently large' a, b and 'sufficiently small' s, without numerical bounds; the existence of admissible parameters is a congruence construction. (iii) No computer verification accompanies this paper, and its folder has no verification directory. (iv) Kato's Theorem B is applied to bindings that need not be homotopy spheres; the text cites it rather than re-proving it. (v) I read the statements and the flagged passages of its nine sections, not every proof.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in either theorem; both rest on classical results invoked after their hypotheses are checked. Paper 1 relies on: Levine's classification of simple spherical knots; Thom–Sebastiani and Sakamoto's integral Seifert formula; Steenbrink, Némethi, Hertling–Mase and Orlik–Randell for the real and integral monodromy identifications; Eichler–Kneser–Platonov strong approximation (Rapinchuk, Theorem 2.3); King and Saeki for the right-equivalence corollary, with Sampaio's source-homeomorphism formulation; and Budur et al. (arXiv v3) for the initial-form corollary. Its finite seed relation is established by a computation, not a proof by hand. Paper 2 relies on: Milnor; Némethi's analytic form of Milnor's theorem; Kato's Theorem B (the text notes it needs no homotopy-sphere hypothesis on the binding, citing Kato p.454 and Durfee); Saeki; the analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4); and strong approximation (Platonov, Rapinchuk). Neither paper depends on the other for its proof; paper 2 says the two arguments are independent. The C³ companion (OpenAIMuConstant2026) is cited in paper 1 only in its family discussion, as far as I read.
zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.direction: disproves the pair form for complex hypersurface germs, in ℂ⁴ (multiplicities 4 and 5) and in ℂᴺ for some N ≥ 8 divisible by eight (multiplicities 2 and 3); the family form is untouched
zariski-multiplicity-conjecture.object: Paper 1: f₁, f₂ are explicit sums of chain polynomials and pure powers with all coefficients 1. Their weights come from an integer relation whose existence the text proves by a finite rank and adjugate computation, and a supplementary explicit relation with 849 nonzero integer coefficients is referenced (verification/support/explicit-relation.json, which I did not open). N is not computed. Paper 2: f₄, f₅ are not written out. They are given as h(p) + w(y^a + z^b) on the smooth fourfold yz = R_s(p,w), with a and b explicit functions of n₀, and then transferred to ℂ⁴ through analytic charts. The germs are constructed, not explicit power series.

virasoro-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts in the family, both about the ordinary descendant Virasoro constraints. (a) “Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization” (dated October 5, 2026) proves a transfer theorem, its main theorem (thm:main). For a smooth connected complex projective variety B and an arbitrary algebraic vector bundle E of rank r ≥ 2, with X = P_B(E) the lines in the fibres, it claims V(B) ⇒ V(X). Here V(Y) means L_k^Y Z_Y = 0 for all k ≥ −1, where Z_Y is the total ordinary descendant potential with full cohomology and integral curve classes, the L_k are Getzler/Katz first-Hodge operators, and the zero-mode constant is C_Y = χ(Y)/16 − str(μ_Y²)/4. The method: an auxiliary space W = P_B(E ⊕ O); localization factoring its ancestor potential through the two fixed theories B and X; a genus-zero shift operator whose spectral branches are λ + h with h^r(h + λ) = y, one branch tending to 0 (B) and r tending to λ (X); quantization of the block modes; continuation between branches by monodromy of the covering h ↦ h^r(h + λ); and fixing the scalar in L_0 by the commutators [L_{-1}, L_1] = −2L_0 and [L_0, L_k] = −kL_k. The manuscript says this covers every genus, each integral curve class and all insertions, including primitive and odd classes, and applies to towers of projective bundles. (b) “Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections” (dated September 24, 2026) claims the unconditional statement (main theorem, thm:main, in its introduction): for every smooth complete intersection X in projective space P^N over C, the ordinary unreduced total descendant potential satisfies L_k^X Z_X = 0 for k ≥ −1, in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from H*(X; C), including primitive and odd classes and with no semisimplicity hypothesis. The method: induction on dimension and then on the complexity Σ(d_i − 1) of the defining degrees, using a degeneration X ⇝ U ∪_D Bl_S M; a tested transport theorem (sew:transport) that carries scalar tests of the Virasoro error through capped chains of ruled pieces; a primitive detector (det:detection) built from a Hodge–Riemann positive form, so that vanishing of the scalar tests forces vanishing of the error on primitive inputs; toric-bundle transfer (ind:toric), taken from Coates–Givental–Tseng, for the projective-bundle pieces; and a deformation argument (ind:deformation) from very general to all smooth members.
virasoro-conjecture.delivers: (a) A conditional transfer and nothing more. If V holds for a smooth connected projective base B, it holds for P_B(E) for every algebraic bundle E of rank ≥ 2, with no splitting or positivity hypothesis, and so for towers of such bundles over any base that satisfies V. The manuscript itself draws two consequences, both resting on cited results: with Okounkov–Pandharipande’s theorem for smooth target curves, V for projective bundles over smooth projective curves and their towers; and, per its introduction, the conclusion for bases with generically semisimple quantum cohomology, which the introduction attributes to Iritani–Koto combined with Givental–Teleman. Its statement of V is the first-Hodge, super, unreduced form with the stated constant, which matches the list’s “half of the Virasoro algebra” formulation. Read with (b), which supplies V for complete intersection bases, (a) would give V for projective bundles over those bases and their towers. That combination is my inference; neither manuscript states it, and (a) does not cite (b). (b) An unconditional proof, but only for one class: smooth complete intersections in P^N, in all genera, all curve classes and with arbitrary insertions including primitive and odd ones. The manuscript says this “resolves the Virasoro conjecture positively for projective-space complete intersections”. Its introduction lists partial earlier results (genus zero by Liu–Tian and Dubrovin–Zhang; Calabi–Yau with H¹ = 0 by Getzler; target curves by Okounkov–Pandharipande; semisimple targets by Givental and Teleman; genus one for Fano complete intersections by Guo–Zhang–Zhou) and says the present argument covers all genera and insertions at once. The list’s statement concerns every smooth projective variety; (b) does not reach beyond projective complete intersections.
virasoro-conjecture.remains: (a) Nothing unconditional: V for the base is the entire input, and the manuscript supplies no base case of its own. If the base is not already known to satisfy V, the conjecture is untouched. For the list’s wording, every smooth projective variety that is not a projective bundle over a base known to satisfy V is outside (a). (b) Every smooth projective variety that is not a complete intersection in projective space, including complete intersections in other ambient spaces and all varieties that are not complete intersections. The list’s “every smooth projective variety” is therefore open beyond the class (b) treats.
virasoro-conjecture.doubts: (a) The theorem is conditional, and the semisimple and curve consequences are stated in the introduction as following from cited results rather than proved in the paper. The two manuscripts disagree on what Okounkov–Pandharipande proved: (a) says it proves the constraints for smooth target curves including odd insertions, while (b) describes the same theorem (OP2003, Theorem 3) as fixed-degree relative constraints for target curves. The curve-base consequence in (a) depends on which description is right, and (a) does not address the difference. The scalar normalization (Lemma cont:commutators) is argued in compressed form: the normal-order constant −½ str(1/4 − μ_Y²) is asserted, the parity sign is checked on two Darboux summands, and the general computation is referred to Givental’s Section 2. Several arguments are signposted forward, for example “the continuation argument will establish its separate finiteness assertion”, and the quantized operators are defined by formal exponential series in a Novikov completion, with the finiteness described rather than fully written out. (b) The argument is long and in several places compressed, with steps justified by “the same argument applies” or “proves directly”. Examples: the coherent single-class lifts of exceptional generators in Lemma ind:blowup-data (justified “as can be seen from” the strict transform of E × A¹); the claim in Lemma ind:degrees that the local monodromy on exceptional surfaces is the identity; and the local constancy of the Hermitian-square test in Lemma ind:deformation, which relies on a Hodge-balance argument written briefly. The source exposition of the product comparison (Abramovich–Fantechi §4.7.1) is stated to assume that each connected component carries a marking or relative root “expressly for simplicity”. The manuscript asserts that its proof extends to unmarked stable components, but does not write that extension in full, and the cohomological evaluation step depends on it (evaluation.tex, Proposition on group products). The tested transport theorem is restricted to admissible singles (algebraic classes, or classes from fixed projective sources through algebraic correspondences). The text explicitly does not assert transport for arbitrary flat Hodge correspondences, so the primitive part is recovered only through the positivity detector on the target itself. The toric-bundle scalar step for k = 0 relies on the first-Hodge L_0 equation with the constant C_Y being the usual Hori equation, which is cited to Getzler rather than reproved. The curve-class statement is first proved on very general fibres and then extended by deformation invariance, and the degree separation depends on Noether–Lefschetz exclusions for surfaces. The positivity argument (det:norm) identifies the conjugate coefficient on a second ordinary replica in a few sentences.; conditional on: (a) The hypothesis V(B) on the base is the theorem’s only assumption. The proof relies on cited results used with their stated hypotheses: Iritani’s equivariant shift-operator theorem (the text asserts W meets its semiprojectivity and weight hypotheses, and that its seminegativity condition is automatic for a complete target); the Coates–Givental quantum Riemann–Roch theorem; Givental’s quantization formalism; Getzler’s super conventions; and Coates–Givental–Tseng’s ancestor localization, which the text adapts and extends to a positive-dimensional orbit family. The introduction’s semisimple and curve consequences rely on Iritani–Koto, Givental–Teleman and Okounkov–Pandharipande respectively. The manuscript does not depend on (b). (b) The theorem assumes nothing beyond the smoothness and projectivity of X. It depends on published inputs used with their stated hypotheses: the Coates–Givental–Tseng toric-bundle theorem (Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.3 of that paper) for projective-bundle pieces; Hu–Li–Ruan’s nonzero projective-space fibre invariants; Abramovich–Fantechi relative theory and configuration spaces (AF2016, AFConfigurations) with the Abramovich–Marcus–Wise comparison; Maulik–Pandharipande’s relative reconstruction; Steenbrink’s limiting mixed Hodge structures and Fujisawa’s ordered model; the Argüz–Bousseau–Pandharipande–Zvonkine splitting geometry and complete-intersection Noether–Lefschetz statement (ABPZ §5.2); Witten–Kontsevich for zero-dimensional targets; and Getzler’s 1999 convention with the Hori-type L_0 equation for the scalar. It does not depend on (a).
virasoro-conjecture.direction: (a) reduces the conjecture for projective bundles to the conjecture for the base (conditional transfer). (b) proves the conjecture for one class: smooth complete intersections in projective space.

hartshornes-conjectures.what_happened: One manuscript, 'The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six' (OpenAI, dated 25 September 2026), claims that every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous (Theorem thm:main, proved in sections/07-conclusion.tex). The route: if the Picard number is at least 2, Kanemitsu's theorem for ρ > n−5 applies. If ρ = 1, the minimal-rational-curve analysis leaves P^6, Q^6, pseudoindex 4 and pseudoindex 5; P^6 and Q^6 are homogeneous. Pseudoindex 4 is settled by an intersection-theoretic argument that rules out Kanemitsu's factorization case (a quadric-bundle contradiction). Pseudoindex 5 is the new step: for a general evaluation fibre F (a threefold) with polarization L, the paper derives u = c1(T_F)·L²/L³ satisfying 32−20u+3u² = 0, using characteristic-number identities and a finite linear-algebra calculation. The sectional-genus formula then forces u = 8/3 and L³ = 3, the variety of minimal rational tangents is the Segre P^1×P^2 in P^5, and Mok's recognition theorem gives Gr(2,5). The same manuscript also proves a compact Kähler corollary (cor:nef-tangent-uniformization): a connected compact Kähler X with analytically nef tangent bundle and dim X − q̃(X) ≤ 6 has ordinary universal cover F×C^q̃(X) with F rational homogeneous. It also states a positive Kähler–Einstein metric for Fano manifolds of dimension at most six with nef tangent bundle (cor:positive-ke). Against the candidates in problem_asks: the manuscript never mentions Hartshorne. The only candidate it bears on is (D), the ample-tangent-bundle conjecture (a smooth projective variety with ample tangent bundle is P^n). The introduction cites Mori 1979 for that ample case and calls the nef question 'natural' from it; it does not restate, prove or extend (D) as such. It makes no claim about (A), (B), (C), (E), (F) or (G).
hartshornes-conjectures.delivers: For candidate (D), only the dimension-six special case of the nef question: the theorem gives rational homogeneity for Fano sixfolds with nef tangent bundle. An ample tangent bundle is nef, so a Fano sixfold with ample tangent bundle falls under the theorem; the text does not draw this consequence, does not show that ampleness of T_X forces the Fano property, and does not identify the homogeneous conclusion with P^6 in the ample case. The manuscript does not say it settles Hartshorne's conjectures or any of the candidates, and its own framing is the Campana–Peternell conjecture, which it states as: every smooth complex Fano variety with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous. It proves that statement for dimension six only, with the Picard-number-one reduction and the pseudoindex-5 Grassmannian identification as the substantive content. For the Kähler corollary, the claim is the universal-cover splitting F×C^q̃ for dim X − q̃(X) ≤ 6 only.
hartshornes-conjectures.remains: If the claim holds, the Campana–Peternell conjecture remains open in dimensions seven and above, and the compact Kähler uniformization remains open when dim X − q̃(X) ≥ 7. For candidate (D), the text adds nothing beyond the dimension-six nef case and draws no consequence for the ample case in other dimensions. Candidates (A), (B), (C), (E), (F) and (G) are untouched.
hartshornes-conjectures.doubts: (1) The pseudoindex-five identity is established by modular rank computations (mod 10007) and an exact check of six rational columns (sections/05-arithmetic.tex). The text says the certifying program is run as verification/verify.py (sections/08-certificate.tex). The reading here relies on that program, which was not read. (2) The Kähler corollary asserts, in one sentence without its own citation, that every positive-dimensional Albanese fibre is a smooth projective Fano manifold with nef tangent bundle (sections/07-conclusion.tex, lines 81–82). The rest of that proof uses this fact. (3) The text never states a consequence for Hartshorne's ample-tangent-bundle conjecture; the link to candidate (D) exists only through the introduction's citation of Mori 1979 and the nef/ample relation.; conditional on: No hypothesis is assumed. The proof uses published results as black boxes: Kanemitsu 2016 Theorem 0.2 (ρ > n−5); Kanemitsu 2017 (minimal-family proposition, Theorem 3.3, Proposition 4.1, Remarks 2.3 and 4.2) for pseudoindex four and the fibre list; Dedieu–Höring 2017 Theorem 1.3 (pseudoindex at least 6); Mok 2008 Theorem 15 and Hwang–Mok 1999 Propositions 1.2.1–1.2.2 (minimal rational tangents); Kebekus 2002 Theorems 3.3–3.4; Mok's recognition theorem (Mok2008Recognition); and Eisenbud–Green–Hulek–Popescu 2006 Theorem 0.1 (varieties of minimal degree). The pseudoindex-five numerical identity 32−20u+3u² = 0 rests on a finite calculation that the text says is verified by a program, verification/verify.py. That file lies outside build/ and was not read here. The Kähler corollary also depends on Demailly–Peternell–Schneider 1994 (Propositions 3.4 and 3.9, Theorem 3.14), Claudon–Höring–Kollár 2013 Theorem 4.4, Fischer–Grauert 1965, Poczobut 2025 Theorem 1.1, and Bien–Brion 1996.
hartshornes-conjectures.direction: proves a case: the Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six (Fano, nef tangent bundle); for candidate (D) only its dimension-six special case

brennan-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts. (1) 'Brennan's conjecture and sharp inverse-square integral means' claims the conjecture on the full stated range: for every simply connected domain W whose boundary in the Riemann sphere has at least two points, and every conformal bijection φ: W→D, the integral of |φ′|^s over W is finite for 4/3 < s < 4. The route is a uniform radial estimate over the normalized univalent class S, M₋₂[f′](r) ≤ C_ε(1−r)^(−1−ε) for all f in S and 1/2 ≤ r < 1, obtained from a transfer-operator growth bound (ρ ≤ 2) that is proved by contradiction. The area statement then follows by passing to f = φ⁻¹ and using the identity ∫_W|φ′|^s dA = ∫_D|f′|^(2−s) dA: Hölder's inequality handles −2 < t < 0, and a separate weighted-area lemma handles 0 < t < 2/3. The same manuscript also claims B_S(−2) = 1, B_S(t) = |t| − 1 for all t ≤ −2, and that the Koebe map shows both open endpoints are sharp. (2) 'A strict inverse-first-power bound for univalent functions' claims a uniform bound over S, M₋₁[f′](r) ≤ C(1−r)^(−1/4+ε) for some 0 < ε < 1/4, with no numerical value for ε. This bears on the Brennan problem only at s = 3 (t = −1): the bound makes the integral of |f′|^(−1) over D uniformly finite, which is the integral of |φ′|^3 over W being finite. The manuscript does not state that consequence; its stated purpose is the bounded-class spectrum at p = −1 (Kraetzer's prediction). It does not claim the full conjecture, and the first manuscript does not use it.
brennan-conjecture.delivers: If the claim is correct, it establishes Brennan's conjecture in the sense the list uses: finiteness of the integral of |φ′|^s over every simply connected W with at least two boundary points in the extended plane, with no boundedness or boundary-regularity assumption, for every 4/3 < s < 4. The manuscript says this is the standard formulation, and its boundary condition is the one the Wikipedia body uses. The problem's statement does not name the subsets; the body's class matches the paper's. The result is a finiteness statement for each W, not a bound, so it answers the bullet's 'estimate' only qualitatively: the area theorem gives no constant and nothing depending only on s. The endpoints 4/3 and 4 are sharp by the Koebe example. Beyond the conjecture, the first manuscript sets B_S(−2) = 1 and proves a uniform radial estimate over S. The s = 3 instance from the second manuscript is a special case of the same statement and adds no new range.
brennan-conjecture.remains: If the claim is correct, none of the open range 4/3 < s < 4 remains for finiteness on simply connected W with at least two boundary points. Not provided: an explicit constant for the area integral, or a bound depending only on s and uniform over W. The text states finiteness per domain. The Hölder step for −2 < t < 0 appears to yield a bound uniform over S from the uniform radial estimate, but the text does not state one. Outside the range the Koebe example gives divergence, so nothing is left to decide there.

Brennan's conjecture asserts that $|\phi'|^s$ is area-integrable for $4/3<s<4$ when $\phi$ conformally maps a simply connected plane domain with nontrivial spherical boundary onto the disk. The formalization establishes this interval, along with area integrability of $|f'|^t$ for univalent disk maps when $-2<t<2/3$.

It also gives the uniform inverse-square radial-mean bound with exponent $-1-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and the spectrum value $B_{\mathcal S}(-2)=1$. The Koebe map and its inverse give divergence at all four boundary exponents.

Kraetzer's proposed integral-means spectrum predicts $B_b(-1)=1/4$ for bounded univalent maps. The formalized result proves $B_b(-1)<1/4$, contradicting that prediction.

The underlying estimate gives constants $0<\varepsilon<1/4$ and $C<\infty$ such that the normalized circular mean of $|f'|^{-1}$ is at most $C(1-r)^{-1/4+\varepsilon}$ for every normalized univalent disk map and $1/2\le r<1$. The bound requires neither bounded image nor boundary regularity, and no numerical value of $\varepsilon$ is specified.

falconers-conjecture.what_happened: One manuscript, 'The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026), is the whole family. Its abstract and main theorem (Theorem thm:main, section 00_introduction) say: for every integer d ≥ 2 and every compact E ⊂ ℝᵈ with dim_H E > d/2, the distance set Δ(E) = {|x−y| : x, y ∈ E} has positive Lebesgue measure, L¹(Δ(E)) > 0. The proof (sections 02–10) takes two separated Frostman probabilities on compact subsets of E, builds decreasing pair filters Γ_N, and approximating distance measures τ_N whose Fourier mass on dyadic shells decays by a power (Proposition 'shell-decay'). A monotone-measure reconstruction lemma then gives a nonzero absolutely continuous limit carried by Δ(E) (Lemma 'monotone-shell', Proposition 'completion'). In odd dimensions an angular projection gain (section 03_angular_gain) and a thin-tube upgrade (Proposition 'thin-upgrade') supply the half-dimension needed; the classical Falconer threshold argument handles the case where the measure charges an affine plane.
falconers-conjecture.delivers: The unpinned positive-measure statement for compact sets: for every d ≥ 2 and every compact E ⊂ ℝᵈ with dim_H E > d/2, L¹(Δ(E)) > 0. This covers d = 2 and every d ≥ 3. The text says it imposes no regularity beyond compactness and the strict dimension inequality (no Ahlfors regularity, equal packing and Hausdorff dimension, product structure or Fourier decay), and that the distances are measured in the original space. The abstract and the text say this resolves the Falconer distance conjecture. Against the list's wording, the claim matches clause (a) (every integer d ≥ 2), clause (c) (positive Lebesgue measure of the distance set) and the strict inequality. It restricts clause (b) from 'sets' to 'compact sets': the introduction restates the conjecture for compact sets and the theorem assumes compactness. The text does not treat non-compact or non-Borel sets and gives no reduction from such a set to a compact subset of the same dimension.
falconers-conjecture.remains: If the claim holds, nothing is left open for compact sets with dim_H E > d/2 in any dimension d ≥ 2. Not covered by the text: (i) sets that are not compact (Borel, analytic or arbitrary sets), which the list's bullet does not exclude; (ii) the endpoint dim_H E = d/2, which the introduction says is 'not asserted'; (iii) the pinned version, where the text says it makes no claim about a single pin at the threshold d/2.

machine_checked.scope: The formalization proves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension. For every integer $d\ge2$ and compact set $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $d/2$, the set $\{\lVert x-y\rVert:x,y\in E\}$ has positive Lebesgue measure. The linked statements include both this all-dimensional result and the earlier planar case.

falconers-conjecture.doubts: (1) The introduction's own history gives Wolff's 4/3 as the best unpinned planar threshold for positive measure. It gives Liu 2026 as a planar result only for Borel sets whose Hausdorff and packing dimensions are equal, and Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang's 5/4 only for a pinned conclusion. The manuscript claims the unpinned planar statement for every compact planar set with dim_H E > 1. The claim is therefore well beyond the thresholds the text itself cites, and the text supports it only with its own argument. (2) In several places the text asks the reader to repeat an earlier argument rather than writing it out: the second-endpoint bound in the restoration-of-mass lemma (asm:retained-measures) holds 'with the endpoints reversed'; the integer-cap lemma (prep:integer-caps) says 'repeat with α and β interchanged'; and the negative-shell bound follows 'the same' way. (3) The final shell inequality comes from a long chain of parameter choices (β, κ, σ, ω, T) with error terms absorbed into 'the stated losses'. The text leaves some of these steps to the choices, for example 'increasing the starting N if necessary'.; conditional on: Yes. The odd-dimensional case (d = 2k−1, k ≥ 2) uses the planar discretized Furstenberg estimate (Theorem ang:furstenberg, stated without proof). The manuscript takes it from Orponen–Shmerkin (OS2023, Theorem 1.3), in the tube formulation of Orponen–Shmerkin–Wang (OSW2024, Definitions 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7), and section 03 calls it 'the only deep input'. The manuscript's claim is conditional on that published theorem being correct as stated. Standard facts (Frostman's lemma, Mattila's Fourier identities, Folland and Simon measure theory) are used without proof. The radial L^p lemma (prep:radial-lp) is adapted from Orponen 2019, but its proof is written out in section 04. kakeya-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts from the openai/math release are matched. (1) “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (dated 23 September 2026) claims that for every ε > 0 and 0 < δ < 1, the radius-δ tube maximal operator K_δ f(ω) = sup over centres a of the average of |f| over the unit tube T_δ(a, ω) satisfies ‖K_δ f‖_{L³(S²)} ≤ C_ε δ^{-ε} ‖f‖_{L³(ℝ³)} for all f in L³(ℝ³). The main theorem matches the abstract. The proof is a contradiction argument on a critical exponent (the proposition “Vanishing at the maximal endpoint”, in the closing section), followed by a reduction from the critical inequality to the maximal bound. The manuscript also states Nikodym maximal estimates on ℝ³ and on local constant-curvature 3-manifolds, and a local curved Kakeya estimate for one fixed translation-invariant phase. It states no Hausdorff or Minkowski dimension conclusion of its own. (2) “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (dated 24 September 2026) claims in its main theorem that if K ⊂ ℝ⁴ contains, for every e ∈ S³, a segment {a_e + te : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} ⊂ K, then dim_H K = 4. No measurability, compactness or regularity is assumed on K or on the family of segments. Its consequences section adds: a bounded such K has lower and upper Minkowski dimension 4; every such K has packing dimension 4; every Kakeya set in ℝᵈ with d ≥ 4 has Hausdorff dimension at least 4, by projection onto a 4-dimensional subspace; if a set E contains a segment in every direction of a set D ⊂ ℝP³, then dim_H E ≥ 1 + dim_H D; and Nikodym sets and fixed-phase curved Kakeya sets in dimension 4 have full dimension.
kakeya-conjecture.delivers: For part (a) of the list's problem at n = 4, the second manuscript gives exactly the list's claim: a set in ℝ⁴ containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension 4. Its statement of the problem matches the list's, and it assumes no compactness or measurability, as the list requires. For part (b) at n = 4, it gives Minkowski dimension 4 only for bounded sets, where lower and upper Minkowski dimension are both 4. The list gives no convention for unbounded sets, and the manuscript does not treat them beyond the packing-dimension statement. So (b) is settled in ℝ⁴ for bounded sets only. For n = 3, the first manuscript gives a quantitative maximal estimate with δ^{-ε} loss at L³ → L³. The list treats n = 3 as already settled by Wang and Zahl (2025), so this is a stronger maximal form in that dimension and not a new set-dimension statement. For n ≥ 5, the second manuscript gives only the lower bound 4 for Hausdorff dimension, not n, and no Minkowski statement.
kakeya-conjecture.remains: (a) For every n ≥ 5, both parts: the list's full conjecture is open, and the manuscript proves only Hausdorff dimension at least 4 there. (b) In ℝ⁴, the Minkowski dimension of unbounded Kakeya sets, which the list leaves without a convention. (c) For n = 3, the list's two parts were already settled by Wang and Zahl (2025), so nothing in the list's wording is new. mahlers-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts in the family claim the symmetric Mahler inequality, and one of them also claims the equality case. (1) 'The symmetric Mahler conjecture and its equality cases' (OpenAI, dated 22 September 2026) claims that every origin-symmetric convex body K in Rⁿ, for every n ≥ 1, satisfies |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ⁿ/n!, with equality exactly for invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes. The inequality is obtained from a lens-based holomorphic mass estimate, which gives a feasible-simplex sum S ≥ 1; since S = (d!/4ᵈ)·∫|Σ_X| dX ≤ (d!/4ᵈ)·|K|·|K°|, this yields |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ᵈ/d!. The equality case lifts K to K ⊕₁ [-1,1] in dimension n+1, builds representations with lens-minimal cost, obtains metric medians for triples in the polar norm, and applies the Hansen–Lima classification of finite-dimensional spaces with the three-ball property. (2) 'Symplectic Balls in Symmetric Polar Products' (same date) claims that for every n ≥ 2 and every origin-symmetric convex body K, the Gromov width of int K × int K° is exactly 4, and that for each 0 < c < 4 there is a smooth symplectic embedding of the standard ball of capacity c (normalised so a ball of radius r has capacity πr²). The upper bound 4 comes from a supporting-slab construction and Gromov's nonsqueezing; the lower bound from a finite-strip construction plus an approximation in the polar body. Its Corollary (symmetric Mahler inequality, every n ≥ 1, with n = 1 checked by hand) follows by comparing volumes: vol(B(c)) = cⁿ/n! ≤ |K|·|K°|, then letting c increase to 4. This paper makes no claim about equality. (3) 'The Mahler Conjecture for General Convex Bodies' (same date) is also in the family, but it does not address the symmetric problem. It proves P(K) ≥ (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)² for all convex bodies, with simplices as the equality cases. Its introduction says the symmetric result is a separate companion theorem and that the general bound does not establish it. Its functional and entropy–transport corollaries lie outside this bullet.
mahlers-conjecture.delivers: Part (1) of problem_asks, the inequality |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ⁿ/n! for every centrally symmetric convex body in every dimension n ≥ 1, is claimed by two routes: directly by the symmetric paper, and via volume comparison from the symplectic paper's Gromov-width theorem. Part (2), the equality characterisation with Hanner polytopes as minimisers, is claimed by the symmetric paper alone. Its abstract says it resolves the symmetric conjecture 'including its equality classification', so by its own account it settles the problem. Its statement matches the list's: the same polar, the same constant, every n, and minimisers that are invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes. The list's cube and cross-polytope are the basic Hanner cases. Since the product is invariant under invertible linear maps, this is the same class. The symplectic paper's abstract also says it 'resolves the symmetric Mahler conjecture positively in every dimension', but its text claims only the inequality. Its own content is stronger than the inequality. It states the exact Gromov width 4 of int K × int K° for every symmetric K with n ≥ 2, and it claims smooth embeddings of every ball with capacity below 4. It does not claim an embedding at capacity exactly 4. Per the paper, earlier results covered only special families or the upper bound: Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover (via a Hofer–Zehnder capacity computation), Karasev for ℓ_p balls, Ramos–Sepe for the cube × cross-polytope, and Vicente for some functional-dual and ordinary polar products.
mahlers-conjecture.remains: If the claims hold, nothing in the bullet's problem_asks remains open. Both the inequality in every dimension and the equality classification are claimed. Outside the bullet, the family leaves the non-symmetric problem to the general-bodies paper, which gives the different constant (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)². The symplectic paper does not claim a ball embedding at capacity exactly 4, and its packing corollary for n ≥ 3 rests on a separate preprint. Neither affects the Mahler statement.

machine_checked.scope:
The symmetric Mahler conjecture predicts $|K||K^\circ|\ge4^n/n!$ for every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$. The formalization establishes this for every $n\ge1$ and characterizes equality exactly by invertible linear images of Hanner bodies, built from intervals using Cartesian products and convex-hull joins.

The nonsymmetric Mahler conjecture and the functional inequalities are not included.

The general Mahler conjecture gives a sharp lower bound for the volume product of a convex body and its polar. For every $n\ge1$ and compact convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with nonempty interior, the formalization proves
$\inf_{z\in\mathrm{int}\,K}|K|\,|(K-z)^\circ|\ge (n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2$.
Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a simplex. The paper's functional inequality is outside this selected statement.

For an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, the formalized result determines the symplectic ball capacity of $\mathrm{int}\,K\times\mathrm{int}\,K^\circ$: its Gromov width is $4$, and every ball of capacity $0<c<4$ embeds symplectically into it. The normalization assigns capacity $\pi r^2$ to a ball of radius $r$.

No boundary smoothness or strict convexity is assumed. An embedding at capacity exactly $4$ is not asserted.

Its introduction says 'We make no claim here about the classification of equality cases', so it covers only the inequality half of the bullet. (b) The equality half is a chain of cited theorems rather than a self-contained proof. The Hansen–Lima statement uses the term '3.2 intersection property', which the text does not define apart from the three-ball lemma and the citation. (c) The sections I read contain no sketch flags or explicit hedges, and no computer-checked steps. The symmetric paper's inequality and equality arguments are presented as complete proofs. The inequality half is the paper's own argument. It starts from a rotation of Gross's conformal map, and its estimates are proved directly. mahlers-conjecture.direction: proves the conjecture: the inequality in all dimensions, and the Hanner equality classification in the symmetric paper
mahlers-conjecture.object: No counterexample. The extremisers are explicit: linear Hanner bodies, built recursively from centred intervals by ℓ∞ sums (Cartesian products) and ℓ1 sums (convex hulls with the origin). The cube and cross-polytope are the basic cases, and the symplectic paper's sharpness remark checks that the cube has product 4ⁿ/n!. In the symplectic paper the phase-space map on the holomorphic domain is given by an explicit integral formula, but the balls inside that domain are produced by an existence argument (a holomorphic-zero ball theorem plus a compactly supported Moser deformation), not written down.

gnrs-conjecture.what_happened: Two manuscripts, both dated 23 September 2026 and attributed to OpenAI, each prove an embedding theorem for weighted shortest-path metrics into real L_1. (1) 'Planar Graph Metrics Embed into L1 with Constant Distortion' proves its Theorem 1.1: there is a universal constant C >= 1 such that every finite connected planar graph with strictly positive real edge lengths admits a map f from its vertices into L_1(Omega, F, mu; R) with d(x,y) <= ||f(x)-f(y)||_1 <= C d(x,y). The proof is a random construction (a column model of the graph, two systems of cut measures, thin-band interpolation, packing bounds) and gives C = 16m/(pb), where m, p, b are fixed constants that do not depend on the graph; I did not trace how m, p, b are fixed. The paper's final section, 'A consequence for almost-embeddable families', states a corollary: for each Lee-Sidiropoulos family AE(g,(k,w),a), every such graph embeds with distortion at most K(g,k,w,a), which depends only on the family's parameters, obtained by combining Theorem 1.1 with the companion bounded-treewidth theorem and Lee-Sidiropoulos's stochastic reduction. It also claims a universal bound on the undirected fractional flow-cut gap for planar graphs with arbitrary demands. (2) 'L1 Embeddings of Graphs of Bounded Treewidth' proves its Theorem 1.1 (labelled thm:main): for every integer k >= 2 there is a finite constant C_k >= 1 such that every finite connected graph with a tree decomposition whose bags have size at most k (treewidth at most k-1) embeds, for every positive edge-length function, into a finite-dimensional real L_1 space with distortion at most C_k. The constant is not computed; the proof is existential, with the lower bound obtained by a compactness argument over a nonprincipal ultrafilter. It also states lambda* <= phi* <= C_k lambda* for the fractional flow-cut gap when bags have size at most k, and says that via the excluded-planar-minor theorem of Robertson and Seymour it also gives a uniform bound for graphs excluding any fixed planar graph as a minor.
gnrs-conjecture.delivers: Both manuscripts describe their results as cases of the GNRS conjecture, not as settling it. Planar paper: for the family of planar graphs, which is a proper minor-closed family, it gives a constant depending on nothing (universal), so it satisfies parts (1) and (2) of the problem for that family; the flow-cut form is also given for planar graphs. The Corollary adds, for each fixed Lee-Sidiropoulos almost-embeddable family, a bound with a constant depending on the family's parameters; the paper does not say whether those families are minor-closed. Treewidth paper: for each fixed bag-size bound k, i.e. each family of graphs of treewidth at most k-1, which is proper minor-closed, it gives a constant depending only on k, satisfying parts (1) and (2) for that family; the flow-cut form is bounded by C_k. It also states that graphs excluding a fixed planar minor are covered, via the cited excluded-planar-minor theorem, which would make it a case for every proper minor-closed family that excludes a planar graph. The manuscripts' statement of the conjecture reads it over proper minor-closed families, which matches the list's reading with 'minor-closed' taken as 'proper minor-closed'. The planar paper's introduction says it 'proves the planar case of the conjecture'; the treewidth paper says it resolves 'the bounded-treewidth case' of the conjecture.
gnrs-conjecture.remains: If the claims are correct, the general statement (part 3: every proper minor-closed family) is still open. The planar paper says that 'the general clique-sum closure required for the full GNRS conjecture is not established here'; the treewidth paper says that extending to gluings along larger complete subgraphs 'remains a further step toward the full conjecture'. Proper minor-closed families not covered by planar graphs, bounded-treewidth graphs, the named almost-embeddable families, or (if its step is accepted) graphs excluding a fixed planar minor are not addressed. The bound for every proper minor-closed family, and its flow-cut form, remain open. The treewidth constant C_k is not explicit, though it depends only on k, as the problem's uniformity clause requires.

machine_checked.scope:
The planar case of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair embedding problem asks for a universal distortion bound in $L_1$. The formalized result gives one constant $C$ for every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths: its weighted shortest-path metric embeds into real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C$. The constant is independent of the number of vertices and the ratios between edge lengths; singleton graphs are included.

The formalized result gives a uniform $L_1$ embedding bound for each bounded-treewidth class. For every bag-size bound $k\ge2$, there is a constant $C(k)$ such that the weighted shortest-path metric of every nonempty finite connected graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most $k$ embeds into finite-dimensional real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C(k)$. Edge lengths may be arbitrary positive real numbers, and the constant is independent of the graph and decomposition size.
